181: #define XSPI_STATUS         (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x110)
182: #define XSPI_CTRL           (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x114)
183: #define XSPI_BCNT           (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x118)
184: 
185: /* XSPI 配置位 */
186: 
187: #define XSPI_CFG_EN         (1 << 0)
188: #define XSPI_CFG_RST        (1 << 1)
189: #define XSPI_CFG_CLK_EN     (1 << 2)
190: 
191: /* XSPI 状态位 */
192: 
193: #define XSPI_STATUS_BUSY    (1 << 0)
194: #define XSPI_STATUS_DONE    (1 << 1)
195: 
196: /* PSRAM 命令 */
197: 
198: #define PSRAM_CMD_RESET     0xFF
199: #define PSRAM_CMD_READ_ID   0x40
200: #define PSRAM_CMD_WRITE_MR  0xC0
201: #define PSRAM_CMD_READ_MR   0x40
202: 
203: /* PSRAM 模式寄存器 */
204: 
205: #define PSRAM_MR0           0x00
206: #define PSRAM_MR4           0x04
207: 
208: static uint32_t d13x_psram_read_efuse(uint32_t reg_addr)
209: {
210:   /* 使能 eFuse 时钟 */
211: 
212:   putreg32(0x1100, EFUSE_CMU_REG);
213: 
214:   /* 读取 eFuse 值 */
215: 
216:   uint32_t val = getreg32(reg_addr);
217: 
218:   /* 关闭 eFuse 时钟 */
219: 
220:   putreg32(0x0, EFUSE_CMU_REG);
221: 
222:   return val;
223: }
224: 
225: static uint32_t d13x_psram_get_size(void)
226: {
227:   uint32_t fuse_218 = d13x_psram_read_efuse(EFUSE_218_REG);
228:   uint8_t mark_id = fuse_218 & 0xFF;
229: 
230:   /* 根据 mark_id 确定 PSRAM 大小 */
231: 
232:   switch (mark_id)
233:     {
234:       case 0x00:  /* force use cfg0 */
235:         return 0;
236:       case 0x01:  /* D131BAS 4M */
237:         return 4 * 1024 * 1024;
238:       case 0x02:  /* D131BBS 8M */
239:       case 0x03:  /* D131CBS 8M */
240:       case 0x04:  /* D131EBS/D133EBS 8M */
241:       case 0x05:  /* D132ENS 8M */
242:       case 0xA1:  /* DR128 8M */
243:       case 0xA2:  /* JYX68 8M */
244:         return 8 * 1024 * 1024;
245:       case 0x06:  /* D131CCS 16M */
246:       case 0x07:  /* D133ECS 16M */
247:         return 16 * 1024 * 1024;
248:       default:
249:         return 8 * 1024 * 1024;  /* 默认 8MB */
250:     }
251: }
252: 
253: static void d13x_xspi_wait_done(void)
254: {
255:   while (!(getreg32(XSPI_STATUS) & XSPI_STATUS_DONE));
256: }
257: 
258: static void d13x_psram_xspi_write_cmd(uint32_t cmd, uint32_t addr,
259:                                        uint8_t *data, int len)
260: {
261:   /* 等待空闲 */
262: 
263:   while (getreg32(XSPI_STATUS) & XSPI_STATUS_BUSY);
264: 
265:   /* 配置命令 */
266: 
267:   putreg32(cmd, XSPI_CMD);
268:   putreg32(addr, XSPI_ADDR);
269:   putreg32(len, XSPI_BCNT);
270: 
271:   /* 写入数据 */
272: 
273:   int i;
274:   for (i = 0; i < len; i++)
275:     {
276:       putreg32(data[i], XSPI_DATA);
277:     }
278: 
279:   /* 启动传输 */
280: 
281:   putreg32(1, XSPI_CTRL);
282: 
283:   /* 等待完成 */
284: 
285:   d13x_xspi_wait_done();
286: }
287: 
288: static void d13x_psram_xspi_read_cmd(uint32_t cmd, uint32_t addr,
289:                                       uint8_t *data, int len)
290: {
291:   /* 等待空闲 */
292: 
293:   while (getreg32(XSPI_STATUS) & XSPI_STATUS_BUSY);
294: 
295:   /* 配置命令 */
296: 
297:   putreg32(cmd, XSPI_CMD);
298:   putreg32(addr, XSPI_ADDR);
299:   putreg32(len, XSPI_BCNT);
300: 
301:   /* 启动传输 */
302: 
303:   putreg32(1, XSPI_CTRL);
304: 
305:   /* 等待完成 */
306: 
307:   d13x_xspi_wait_done();
308: 
309:   /* 读取数据 */
310: 
311:   int i;
312:   for (i = 0; i < len; i++)
313:     {
314:       data[i] = (uint8_t)getreg32(XSPI_DATA);
315:     }
316: }
317: 
318: static void d13x_psram_device_reset(void)
319: {
320:   /* 发送复位命令 */
321: 
322:   uint8_t cmd = PSRAM_CMD_RESET;
323:   d13x_psram_xspi_write_cmd(0xFF, 0, &cmd, 1);
324: }
325: 
326: static void d13x_psram_device_init(void)
327: {
328:   uint8_t data;
329: 
330:   /* 读取 MR4 检查当前配置 */
331: 
332:   d13x_psram_xspi_read_cmd(PSRAM_CMD_READ_MR, PSRAM_MR4, &data, 1);
333: 
334:   /* 配置 MR0: 设置 burst 长度和延迟 */
335: 
336:   data = 0x19;  /* Burst Length = 32, Latency = 3 */
337:   d13x_psram_xspi_write_cmd(PSRAM_CMD_WRITE_MR, PSRAM_MR0, &data, 1);
338: 
339:   /* 配置 MR4: 使能 XIP */
340: 
341:   data = 0x80;  /* Enable XIP */
342:   d13x_psram_xspi_write_cmd(PSRAM_CMD_WRITE_MR, PSRAM_MR4, &data, 1);
343: }
344: 
345: static void d13x_psram_xip_enable(void)
346: {
347:   /* 配置 XSPI 控制器为 XIP 模式 */
348: 
349:   uint32_t cfg = getreg32(XSPI_CFG);
350:   cfg |= (1 << 8);  /* XIP 模式 */
351:   cfg |= (1 << 9);  /* DDR 模式 */
352:   putreg32(cfg, XSPI_CFG);
353: 
354:   /* 配置 XIP 参数 */
355: 
356:   putreg32(0x00000000, XSPI_CFG2);  /* XIP 基地址 */
357:   putreg32(0x00000000, XSPI_CFG3);  /* XIP 大小 */
358: }
359: 
360: static uint32_t d13x_psram_verify(void)
361: {
362:   volatile uint32_t *psram = (volatile uint32_t *)D13X_PSRAM_BASE;
363:   uint32_t psram_size = d13x_psram_get_size();
364: 
365:   if (psram_size == 0)
366:     return 0;
367: 
368:   /* 写入测试模式 */
369: 
370:   psram[0] = 0x12345678;
371:   psram[1] = 0x9ABCDEF0;
372: 
373:   /* 读取并验证 */
374: 
375:   if (psram[0] != 0x12345678)
376:     return 0;
377: 
378:   if (psram[1] != 0x9ABCDEF0)
379:     return 0;
380: 
381:   /* 清除测试数据 */
382: 
383:   psram[0] = 0;
384:   psram[1] = 0;
385: 
386:   return psram_size;
387: }
388: 
389: static void d13x_psram_init(void)
390: {
391:   /* 首先验证 PSRAM 是否已初始化 */
392: 
393:   uint32_t psram_size = d13x_psram_verify();
394: 
395:   if (psram_size > 0)
396:     {
397:       /* PSRAM 已初始化，验证成功 */
398:       return;
399:     }
400: 
401:   /* PSRAM 未初始化，执行完整初始化 */
402: 
403:   /* 1. 使能 XSPI 时钟 (CMU_BASE + 0x460) */
404: 
405:   uint32_t reg = getreg32(D13X_CMU_BASE + 0x460);
406:   reg |= (1 << 13) | (1 << 12) | (1 << 8);
407:   putreg32(reg, D13X_CMU_BASE + 0x460);
408: 
409:   /* 2. 复位 XSPI 控制器 */
410: 
411:   putreg32(XSPI_CFG_RST, XSPI_CFG);
412:   while (getreg32(XSPI_CFG) & XSPI_CFG_RST);
413: 
414:   /* 3. 使能 XSPI 控制器 */
415: 
416:   putreg32(XSPI_CFG_EN | XSPI_CFG_CLK_EN, XSPI_CFG);
417: 
418:   /* 4. 复位 PSRAM 设备 */
419: 
420:   d13x_psram_device_reset();
421: 
422:   /* 5. 配置 PSRAM 设备 */
423: 
424:   d13x_psram_device_init();
425: 
426:   /* 6. 使能 XIP 模式 */
427: 
428:   d13x_psram_xip_enable();
429: 
430:   /* 7. 验证初始化 */
431: 
432:   d13x_psram_verify();
433: }
434: 
435: /****************************************************************************
436:  * 看门狗处理 (D13x)
437:  * WDT 基地址: 0x19000000 (来源: luban-lite aic_soc.h)
438:  ****************************************************************************/
439: 
440: static void d13x_watchdog_init(void)
441: {
442:   /* 禁用看门狗，防止启动过程中被复位
443:    * 写 WDOG_CTL 禁用看门狗 (bit 0 = EN, 写 0 禁用)
444:    */
445: 
446:   putreg32(0, WDOG_CTL);
447: }

450:  * Public Functions
451:  ****************************************************************************/
452: 
453: /****************************************************************************
454:  * Name: __start
455:  *
456:  * Description:
457:  *   D13x 系统复位入口
458:  *
459:  ****************************************************************************/

461: void __start(void)
462: {
463:   /* 清除 BSS 段 */
464: 
465:   uint32_t *ptr;
466: 
467:   for (ptr = _sbss; ptr < _ebss; ptr++)
468:     {
469:       *ptr = 0;
470:     }
471: 
472:   /* 拷贝 .data 段 */
473: 
474:   for (ptr = _sdata; ptr < _edata; ptr++)
475:     {
476:       *ptr = *(_eronly + (ptr - _sdata));
477:     }
478: 
479:   /* 禁用看门狗 */
480: 
481:   d13x_watchdog_init();
482: 
483:   /* 初始化系统时钟 */
484: 
485:   d13x_clock_init();
486: 
487:   /* 初始化 UART0 */
488: 
489:   d13x_uart_init();
490: 
491:   /* 初始化 PSRAM */
492: 
493:   d13x_psram_init();
494:

496: 
497:   putreg32('D', D13X_UART0_BASE + UART_RBR_THR_DLL);
498: 
499:   /* 启动 NuttX */
500: 
501:   nx_start();
502: 
503:   /* 不应到达此处 */
504: 
505:   for (; ; );

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * D13x tinySPL Bootloader - system.c
3:  *
4:  * 完整的系统初始化：时钟、UART、SPI Flash、PSRAM
5:  * 地址来源: luban-lite aic_soc.h + D13x User Manual
6:  *
7:  ****************************************************************************/
8: 
9: #include <stdint.h>
10: #include "d13x_boot.h"
11: 
12: /****************************************************************************
13:  * 寄存器访问宏
14:  ****************************************************************************/
15: 
16: #define getreg32(a)     (*(volatile uint32_t *)(a))
17: #define putreg32(v,a)   (*(volatile uint32_t *)(a) = (v))
18: 
19: /****************************************************************************
20:  * 外设基地址 (来源: luban-lite aic_soc.h)
21:  ****************************************************************************/
22: 
23: #define CMU_BASE        0x18020000
24: #define GPIO_BASE       0x18700000
25: #define UART0_BASE      0x18710000
26: #define XSPI_BASE       0x10300000  /* XSPI PSRAM 控制器 */
27: #define QSPI0_BASE      0x10400000  /* QSPI0 SPI Flash */
28: #define WDT_BASE        0x19000000  /* Watchdog */
29: #define SID_BASE        0x19010000  /* eFuse */
30: 
31: /****************************************************************************
32:  * PSRAM 配置 (D13x)
33:  ****************************************************************************/
34: 
35: #define PSRAM_BASE          0x40000000
36: #define PSRAM_SIZE          (8 * 1024 * 1024)  /* 8MB */
37: 
38: /* eFuse 寄存器 */
39: 
40: #define EFUSE_CMU_REG       (CMU_BASE + 0x904)
41: #define EFUSE_218_REG       (SID_BASE + 0x218)
42: #define EFUSE_224_REG       (SID_BASE + 0x224)
43: 
44: /* PSRAM 芯片 ID */
45: 
46: #define PSRAM_CHIP_APS3208K 0x80c9
47: #define PSRAM_CHIP_SCKW18   0xc59a
48: #define PSRAM_CHIP_APS12816 0xdd8d
49: 
50: /****************************************************************************
51:  * 时钟系统 (CMU)
52:  ****************************************************************************/
53: 
54: void d13x_clock_init(void)
55: {
56:   uint32_t reg;
57: 
58:   /* 打开 24MHz 振荡器 */
59: 
60:   reg = getreg32(CMU_BASE + 0x0A4);
61:   reg |= (1 << 1);
62:   putreg32(reg, CMU_BASE + 0x0A4);
63: 
64:   /* PLL 公共电路 LDO */
65: 
66:   reg = getreg32(CMU_BASE + 0x0A0);
67:   reg |= (1 << 31) | (1 << 0);
68:   putreg32(reg, CMU_BASE + 0x0A0);
69: 
70:   /* PLL_INT1 → 1.2GHz */
71: 
72:   putreg32(0x240C4040, CMU_BASE + 0x044);
73:   while (!(getreg32(CMU_BASE + 0x044) & (1 << 17)));
74: 
75:   /* PLL_INT0 → 480MHz */
76: 
77:   putreg32(0x240C4040, CMU_BASE + 0x040);
78:   while (!(getreg32(CMU_BASE + 0x040) & (1 << 17)));
79: 
80:   /* 总线时钟 */
81: 
82:   putreg32(0x00000001, CMU_BASE + 0x100);
83:   putreg32(0x00000001, CMU_BASE + 0x120);
84:   putreg32(0x00000100, CMU_BASE + 0x200);
85: 
86:   /* GPIO/UART 时钟 */
87: 
88:   reg = getreg32(CMU_BASE + 0x83C);
89:   reg |= (1 << 12) | (1 << 13);
90:   putreg32(reg, CMU_BASE + 0x83C);
91:   putreg32(0x00001001, CMU_BASE + 0x840);
92: 
93:   /* QSPI0 时钟: 释放复位 + 使能总线时钟 + 使能模块时钟 */
94: 
95:   putreg32((1 << 13) | (1 << 12) | (1 << 8), CMU_BASE + 0x460);
96: }
97: 
98: /****************************************************************************
99:  * UART 驱动 (UART0 基地址: 0x18710000)
100:  ****************************************************************************/
101: 
102: void d13x_uart_init(void)
103: {
104:   uint32_t divisor = 60000000 / (16 * 115200);
105:   putreg32(0, UART0_BASE + 0x0C);           /* LCR = 0 */
106:   putreg32(divisor & 0xFF, UART0_BASE + 0x00);  /* DLL */
107:   putreg32((divisor >> 8) & 0xFF, UART0_BASE + 0x04);  /* DLH */
108:   putreg32(0x07, UART0_BASE + 0x08);        /* FIFO: enable + reset */
109:   putreg32(0x03, UART0_BASE + 0x0C);        /* LCR: 8N1 */
110: }
111: 
112: void d13x_putc(char ch)
113: {
114:   while (!(getreg32(UART0_BASE + 0x14) & (1 << 5)));  /* LSR.THRE */
115:   putreg32((uint32_t)ch, UART0_BASE + 0x00);
116: }
117: 
118: int d13x_getc(void)
119: {
120:   while (!(getreg32(UART0_BASE + 0x14) & (1 << 0)));  /* LSR.DR */
121:   return (int)(getreg32(UART0_BASE + 0x00) & 0xFF);
122: }
123: 
124: int d13x_uart_rxready(void)
125: {
126:   return (getreg32(UART0_BASE + 0x14) & (1 << 0)) != 0;
127: }
128: 
129: /****************************************************************************
130:  * QSPI 控制器 (D13x)
131:  * QSPI0 基地址: 0x10400000 (来源: luban-lite aic_soc.h)
132:  ****************************************************************************/
133: 
134: #define QSPI_BASE      QSPI0_BASE
135: #define QSPI_VER       (QSPI_BASE + 0x000)
136: #define QSPI_CFG       (QSPI_BASE + 0x004)
137: #define QSPI_TCFG      (QSPI_BASE + 0x008)
138: #define QSPI_ICR       (QSPI_BASE + 0x010)
139: #define QSPI_ISTS      (QSPI_BASE + 0x014)
140: #define QSPI_FCTL      (QSPI_BASE + 0x018)
141: #define QSPI_FSTS      (QSPI_BASE + 0x01C)
142: #define QSPI_CCFG      (QSPI_BASE + 0x024)
143: #define QSPI_TXD       (QSPI_BASE + 0x200)
144: #define QSPI_RXD       (QSPI_BASE + 0x300)
145: 
146: /* QSPI_CFG bits */
147: 
148: #define QSPI_CFG_EN        (1 << 0)
149: #define QSPI_CFG_MASTER    (1 << 1)
150: #define QSPI_CFG_RST       (1 << 31)
151: 
152: /* QSPI_TCFG bits */
153: 
154: #define QSPI_TCFG_CPHA     (1 << 0)
155: #define QSPI_TCFG_CPOL     (1 << 1)
156: #define QSPI_TCFG_CS_LOW   (0 << 7)
157: #define QSPI_TCFG_CS_HIGH  (1 << 7)
158: #define QSPI_TCFG_CS_SW    (1 << 6)
159: #define QSPI_TCFG_START    (1 << 31)
160: 
161: /* QSPI_FSTS bits */
162: 
163: #define QSPI_FSTS_TD       (1 << 12)
164: #define QSPI_FSTS_TF_EMP   (1 << 5)
165: #define QSPI_FSTS_RF_RDY   (1 << 0)
166: 
167: static void d13x_spi_init(void)
168: {
169:   /* 复位控制器 */
170: 
171:   putreg32(QSPI_CFG_RST, QSPI_CFG);
172:   while (getreg32(QSPI_CFG) & QSPI_CFG_RST);
173: 
174:   /* 使能控制器 + 主机模式 */
175: 
176:   putreg32(QSPI_CFG_EN | QSPI_CFG_MASTER, QSPI_CFG);
177: 
178:   /* 时钟分频: SPI_CLK = src_clk / (2 * (CKDIV2 + 1))
179:    * src=480MHz, CKDIV2=15 → SPI_CLK = 480/(2*16) = 15MHz */
180: 
181:   putreg32(15, QSPI_CCFG);
182: 
183:   /* 传输配置: Mode 0 (CPOL=0, CPHA=0), 软件控制CS */
184: 
185:   putreg32(QSPI_TCFG_CS_SW | QSPI_TCFG_CS_HIGH, QSPI_TCFG);
186: 
187:   /* 复位 FIFO */
188: 
189:   putreg32((1 << 31) | (1 << 15), QSPI_FCTL);
190: }
191: 
192: static void d13x_spi_cs(int assert)
193: {
194:   uint32_t reg = getreg32(QSPI_TCFG);
195:   if (assert)
196:     reg &= ~QSPI_TCFG_CS_HIGH;
197:   else
198:     reg |= QSPI_TCFG_CS_HIGH;
199:   putreg32(reg, QSPI_TCFG);
200: }
201: 
202: static void d13x_spi_txrx(uint8_t *tx, uint8_t *rx, int len)
203: {
204:   int i;
205:   for (i = 0; i < len; i++)
206:     {
207:       /* 写入 TX FIFO */
208: 
209:       putreg32(tx ? tx[i] : 0, QSPI_TXD);
210: 
211:       /* 启动传输 */
212: 
213:       uint32_t tcfg = getreg32(QSPI_TCFG);
214:       putreg32(tcfg | QSPI_TCFG_START, QSPI_TCFG);
215: 
216:       /* 等待传输完成 */
217: 
218:       while (!(getreg32(QSPI_FSTS) & QSPI_FSTS_TD));
219: 
220:       /* 清除 TD 标志 (W1C) */
221: 
222:       putreg32(QSPI_FSTS_TD, QSPI_ISTS);
223: 
224:       /* 读取 RX FIFO */
225: 
226:       if (rx)
227:         rx[i] = (uint8_t)getreg32(QSPI_RXD);
228:     }
229: }

231: /****************************************************************************
232:  * SPI NOR Flash 驱动
233:  ****************************************************************************/
234: 
235: #define FLASH_WRITE_ENABLE    0x06
236: #define FLASH_READ_STATUS     0x05
237: #define FLASH_READ_DATA       0x03
238: #define FLASH_PAGE_PROGRAM    0x02
239: #define FLASH_SECTOR_ERASE    0x20
240: #define FLASH_READ_ID         0x9F
241: 
242: static void d13x_flash_write_enable(void)
243: {
244:   uint8_t cmd = FLASH_WRITE_ENABLE;
245:   d13x_spi_cs(1);
246:   d13x_spi_txrx(&cmd, 0, 1);
247:   d13x_spi_cs(0);
248: }
249: 
250: static void d13x_flash_wait_busy(void)
251: {
252:   uint8_t cmd = FLASH_READ_STATUS;
253:   uint8_t status;
254:   do {
255:     d13x_spi_cs(1);
256:     d13x_spi_txrx(&cmd, 0, 1);
257:     d13x_spi_txrx(0, &status, 1);
258:     d13x_spi_cs(0);
259:   } while (status & 0x01);
260: }
261: 
262: void d13x_flash_write(uint32_t addr, uint8_t *data, int len)
263: {
264:   uint8_t cmd[4];
265:   cmd[0] = FLASH_PAGE_PROGRAM;
266:   cmd[1] = (addr >> 16) & 0xFF;
267:   cmd[2] = (addr >> 8) & 0xFF;
268:   cmd[3] = addr & 0xFF;
269: 
270:   d13x_flash_write_enable();
271:   d13x_spi_cs(1);
272:   d13x_spi_txrx(cmd, 0, 4);
273:   d13x_spi_txrx(data, 0, len);
274:   d13x_spi_cs(0);
275:   d13x_flash_wait_busy();
276: }
277: 
278: void d13x_flash_erase_sector(uint32_t addr)
279: {
280:   uint8_t cmd[4];
281:   cmd[0] = FLASH_SECTOR_ERASE;
282:   cmd[1] = (addr >> 16) & 0xFF;
283:   cmd[2] = (addr >> 8) & 0xFF;
284:   cmd[3] = addr & 0xFF;
285: 
286:   d13x_flash_write_enable();
287:   d13x_spi_cs(1);
288:   d13x_spi_txrx(cmd, 0, 4);
289:   d13x_spi_cs(0);
290:   d13x_flash_wait_busy();
291: }
292: 
293: uint32_t d13x_flash_read_id(void)
294: {
295:   uint8_t cmd = FLASH_READ_ID;
296:   uint8_t id[3];

162:   /* 配置 8N1: 8 数据位, 1 停止位, 无校验 */
163: 
164:   putreg32(0x03, D13X_UART0_BASE + UART_LCR);
165: }

167: /****************************************************************************
168:  * PSRAM 驱动 (D13x)
169:  * XSPI 基地址: 0x10300000 (来源: luban-lite aic_soc.h)
170:  ****************************************************************************/
171: 
172: /* XSPI 控制器寄存器 */
173: 
174: #define XSPI_CFG            (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x000)
175: #define XSPI_TIMING         (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x004)
176: #define XSPI_CFG2           (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x008)
177: #define XSPI_CMD            (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x100)
178: #define XSPI_ADDR           (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x104)
179: #define XSPI_DATA           (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x108)
180: #define XSPI_CFG3           (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x10C)
181: #define XSPI_STATUS         (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x110)
182: #define XSPI_CTRL           (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x114)
183: #define XSPI_BCNT           (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x118)
184: 
185: /* XSPI 配置位 */
186: 
187: #define XSPI_CFG_EN         (1 << 0)
188: #define XSPI_CFG_RST        (1 << 1)
189: #define XSPI_CFG_CLK_EN     (1 << 2)
190: 
191: /* XSPI 状态位 */
192: 
193: #define XSPI_STATUS_BUSY    (1 << 0)
194: #define XSPI_STATUS_DONE    (1 << 1)
195: 
196: /* PSRAM 命令 */
197: 
198: #define PSRAM_CMD_RESET     0xFF
199: #define PSRAM_CMD_READ_ID   0x40
200: #define PSRAM_CMD_WRITE_MR  0xC0
201: #define PSRAM_CMD_READ_MR   0x40
202: 
203: /* PSRAM 模式寄存器 */
204: 
205: #define PSRAM_MR0           0x00
206: #define PSRAM_MR4           0x04
207: 
208: static uint32_t d13x_psram_read_efuse(uint32_t reg_addr)
209: {
210:   /* 使能 eFuse 时钟 */
211: 
212:   putreg32(0x1100, EFUSE_CMU_REG);
213: 
214:   /* 读取 eFuse 值 */
215: 
216:   uint32_t val = getreg32(reg_addr);
217: 
218:   /* 关闭 eFuse 时钟 */
219: 
220:   putreg32(0x0, EFUSE_CMU_REG);
221: 
222:   return val;
223: }
224: 
225: static uint32_t d13x_psram_get_size(void)
226: {
227:   uint32_t fuse_218 = d13x_psram_read_efuse(EFUSE_218_REG);
228:   uint8_t mark_id = fuse_218 & 0xFF;
229: 
230:   /* 根据 mark_id 确定 PSRAM 大小 */
231: 
232:   switch (mark_id)
233:     {
234:       case 0x00:  /* force use cfg0 */
235:         return 0;
236:       case 0x01:  /* D131BAS 4M */
237:         return 4 * 1024 * 1024;
238:       case 0x02:  /* D131BBS 8M */
239:       case 0x03:  /* D131CBS 8M */
240:       case 0x04:  /* D131EBS/D133EBS 8M */
241:       case 0x05:  /* D132ENS 8M */
242:       case 0xA1:  /* DR128 8M */
243:       case 0xA2:  /* JYX68 8M */
244:         return 8 * 1024 * 1024;
245:       case 0x06:  /* D131CCS 16M */
246:       case 0x07:  /* D133ECS 16M */
247:         return 16 * 1024 * 1024;
248:       default:
249:         return 8 * 1024 * 1024;  /* 默认 8MB */
250:     }
251: }
252: 
253: static void d13x_xspi_wait_done(void)
254: {
255:   while (!(getreg32(XSPI_STATUS) & XSPI_STATUS_DONE));
256: }
257: 
258: static void d13x_psram_xspi_write_cmd(uint32_t cmd, uint32_t addr,
259:                                        uint8_t *data, int len)
260: {
261:   /* 等待空闲 */
262: 
263:   while (getreg32(XSPI_STATUS) & XSPI_STATUS_BUSY);
264: 
265:   /* 配置命令 */
266: 
267:   putreg32(cmd, XSPI_CMD);
268:   putreg32(addr, XSPI_ADDR);
269:   putreg32(len, XSPI_BCNT);
270: 
271:   /* 写入数据 */
272: 
273:   int i;
274:   for (i = 0; i < len; i++)
275:     {
276:       putreg32(data[i], XSPI_DATA);
277:     }
278: 
279:   /* 启动传输 */
280: 
281:   putreg32(1, XSPI_CTRL);
282: 
283:   /* 等待完成 */
284: 
285:   d13x_xspi_wait_done();
286: }
287: 
288: static void d13x_psram_xspi_read_cmd(uint32_t cmd, uint32_t addr,
289:                                       uint8_t *data, int len)
290: {
291:   /* 等待空闲 */
292: 
293:   while (getreg32(XSPI_STATUS) & XSPI_STATUS_BUSY);
294: 
295:   /* 配置命令 */
296: 
297:   putreg32(cmd, XSPI_CMD);
298:   putreg32(addr, XSPI_ADDR);
299:   putreg32(len, XSPI_BCNT);
300: 
301:   /* 启动传输 */
302: 
303:   putreg32(1, XSPI_CTRL);
304: 
305:   /* 等待完成 */
306: 
307:   d13x_xspi_wait_done();
308: 
309:   /* 读取数据 */
310: 
311:   int i;
312:   for (i = 0; i < len; i++)
313:     {
314:       data[i] = (uint8_t)getreg32(XSPI_DATA);
315:     }
316: }
317: 
318: static void d13x_psram_device_reset(void)
319: {
320:   /* 发送复位命令 */
321: 
322:   uint8_t cmd = PSRAM_CMD_RESET;
323:   d13x_psram_xspi_write_cmd(0xFF, 0, &cmd, 1);
324: }
325: 
326: static void d13x_psram_device_init(void)
327: {
328:   uint8_t data;
329: 
330:   /* 读取 MR4 检查当前配置 */
331: 
332:   d13x_psram_xspi_read_cmd(PSRAM_CMD_READ_MR, PSRAM_MR4, &data, 1);
333: 
334:   /* 配置 MR0: 设置 burst 长度和延迟 */
335: 
336:   data = 0x19;  /* Burst Length = 32, Latency = 3 */
337:   d13x_psram_xspi_write_cmd(PSRAM_CMD_WRITE_MR, PSRAM_MR0, &data, 1);
338: 
339:   /* 配置 MR4: 使能 XIP */
340: 
341:   data = 0x80;  /* Enable XIP */
342:   d13x_psram_xspi_write_cmd(PSRAM_CMD_WRITE_MR, PSRAM_MR4, &data, 1);
343: }
344: 
345: static void d13x_psram_xip_enable(void)
346: {
347:   /* 配置 XSPI 控制器为 XIP 模式 */
348: 
349:   uint32_t cfg = getreg32(XSPI_CFG);
350:   cfg |= (1 << 8);  /* XIP 模式 */
351:   cfg |= (1 << 9);  /* DDR 模式 */
352:   putreg32(cfg, XSPI_CFG);
353: 
354:   /* 配置 XIP 参数 */
355: 
356:   putreg32(0x00000000, XSPI_CFG2);  /* XIP 基地址 */
357:   putreg32(0x00000000, XSPI_CFG3);  /* XIP 大小 */
358: }
359: 
360: static uint32_t d13x_psram_verify(void)
361: {
362:   volatile uint32_t *psram = (volatile uint32_t *)D13X_PSRAM_BASE;
363:   uint32_t psram_size = d13x_psram_get_size();
364: 
365:   if (psram_size == 0)
366:     return 0;
367: 
368:   /* 写入测试模式 */
369: 
370:   psram[0] = 0x12345678;
371:   psram[1] = 0x9ABCDEF0;
372: 
373:   /* 读取并验证 */
374: 
375:   if (psram[0] != 0x12345678)
376:     return 0;
377: 
378:   if (psram[1] != 0x9ABCDEF0)
379:     return 0;
380: 
381:   /* 清除测试数据 */
382: 
383:   psram[0] = 0;
384:   psram[1] = 0;
385: 
386:   return psram_size;
387: }
388: 
389: static void d13x_psram_init(void)
390: {
391:   /* 首先验证 PSRAM 是否已初始化 */
392: 
393:   uint32_t psram_size = d13x_psram_verify();
394: 
395:   if (psram_size > 0)
396:     {
397:       /* PSRAM 已初始化，验证成功 */
398:       return;
399:     }
400: 
401:   /* PSRAM 未初始化，执行完整初始化 */
402: 
403:   /* 1. 使能 XSPI 时钟 (CMU_BASE + 0x460) */
404: 
405:   uint32_t reg = getreg32(D13X_CMU_BASE + 0x460);
406:   reg |= (1 << 13) | (1 << 12) | (1 << 8);
407:   putreg32(reg, D13X_CMU_BASE + 0x460);
408: 
409:   /* 2. 复位 XSPI 控制器 */
410: 
411:   putreg32(XSPI_CFG_RST, XSPI_CFG);
412:   while (getreg32(XSPI_CFG) & XSPI_CFG_RST);
413: 
414:   /* 3. 使能 XSPI 控制器 */
415: 
416:   putreg32(XSPI_CFG_EN | XSPI_CFG_CLK_EN, XSPI_CFG);
417: 
418:   /* 4. 复位 PSRAM 设备 */
419: 
420:   d13x_psram_device_reset();
421: 
422:   /* 5. 配置 PSRAM 设备 */
423: 
424:   d13x_psram_device_init();
425: 
426:   /* 6. 使能 XIP 模式 */
427: 
428:   d13x_psram_xip_enable();
429: 
430:   /* 7. 验证初始化 */
431: 
432:   d13x_psram_verify();
433: }

435: /****************************************************************************
436:  * 看门狗处理 (D13x)
437:  * WDT 基地址: 0x19000000 (来源: luban-lite aic_soc.h)
438:  ****************************************************************************/
439: 
440: static void d13x_watchdog_init(void)
441: {
442:   /* 禁用看门狗，防止启动过程中被复位
443:    * 写 WDOG_CTL 禁用看门狗 (bit 0 = EN, 写 0 禁用)
444:    */
445: 
446:   putreg32(0, WDOG_CTL);
447: }

461: void __start(void)
462: {
463:   /* 清除 BSS 段 */
464: 
465:   uint32_t *ptr;
466: 
467:   for (ptr = _sbss; ptr < _ebss; ptr++)
468:     {
469:       *ptr = 0;
470:     }
471: 
472:   /* 拷贝 .data 段 */
473: 
474:   for (ptr = _sdata; ptr < _edata; ptr++)
475:     {
476:       *ptr = *(_eronly + (ptr - _sdata));
477:     }
478: 
479:   /* 禁用看门狗 */
480: 
481:   d13x_watchdog_init();
482: 
483:   /* 初始化系统时钟 */
484: 
485:   d13x_clock_init();
486: 
487:   /* 初始化 UART0 */
488: 
489:   d13x_uart_init();

492:

496: 
497:   putreg32('D', D13X_UART0_BASE + UART_RBR_THR_DLL);
498: 
499:   /* 启动 NuttX */
500: 
501:   nx_start();
502: 
503:   /* 不应到达此处 */
504: 
505:   for (; ; );

The comment in the struct description uses "offset" but means position within the struct when viewed as individual bytes - however the comment shows +0x004, +0x008, +0x00C which would be word offsets. ```

But the actual luban-lite struct core_rv32.h says:

```
 *   uint8_t CTL;   offset: 0x00C
```

Wait, luban-lite says offsets 0x000, 0x004, 0x008, 0x00C. But these are uint8_t members... In the actual struct, they're packed as individual bytes. The "Offset" comments in the luban-lite header are also misleading - they say offset 0x004 for IE, but IE is the second byte in the struct. So these offsets must be wrong in the luban-lite source too, or they're using some different interpretation.

Actually, looking more carefully at the luban-lite CLIC_INT_Control struct:
```c
typedef struct
{
    __IOM uint8_t IP;  /*!< Offset: 0x000 (R/W) Interrupt set pending */
    __IOM uint8_t IE;  /*!< Offset: 0x004 (R/W) Interrupt set enable */
    __IOM uint8_t ATTR;/*!< Offset: 0x008 (R/W) Interrupt set attribute */
    __IOM uint8_t CTL; /*!< Offset: 0x00C (R/W) Interrupt control */
} CLIC_INT_Control;
```

These are CMSIS-style offset comments. In CMSIS, the offset comment is typically the byte offset within the register block. But here we have uint8_t members, so the actual offsets would be +0, +1, +2, +3 in a packed struct. The comments in the luban-lite header appear to be **wrong** - they list 0x004, 0x008, 0x00C for 1-byte members.

But looking at how the CLIC_Type struct is actually used: `CLIC->CLICINT[i].IP`, `CLIC->CLICINT[i].IE`, etc. - the compiler handles the offsets. The struct has `CLIC_INT_Control CLICINT[4096]` starting at offset 0x1000, and each CLIC_INT_Control is 4 bytes (4 uint8_t members).

So the actual byte layout per interrupt entry is:
- IP at +0
- IE at +1
- ATTR at +2
- CTL at +3

And in artinchip_irq.c, the code correctly accesses:
- IP: `D13X_CLIC_INT_BASE + irq * 4 + 0`
- IE: `D13X_CLIC_INT_BASE + irq * 4 + 1`

### Check 2: defconfig RAM_SIZE vs Linker Script SRAM Length

- **defconfig** (`CONFIG_RAM_SIZE`): `1048576` (= 0x100000 = 1 MiB)
- **Board linker script** (`ld.script`, line 12): `LENGTH = 1M`
- **Bootloader linker script** (`linker.ld`, line 16): `LENGTH = 768K`

**PASS** -- The defconfig and the board linker script both specify 1 MiB of SRAM. The bootloader linker script intentionally reserves only 768 KiB, which is a deliberate partitioning (bootloader code runs from the low portion of SRAM, leaving the upper 256 KiB for the NuttX image). This is a correct and expected design pattern where the bootloader pre-allocates its footprint before jumping to the firmware.

I now have all the source material. Here is the full verification report.

---

## Verification Report: OpenVela D13x Port vs. Luban-Lite Reference

### 1. CLIC Register Layout — `artinchip_irq.c` vs. luban-lite `core_rv32.h`

**Overall structure: MATCHES**

| Field | OpenVela (artinchip_irq.c) | Luban-Lite (core_rv32.h) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLICCFG offset | 0x000 | 0x000 | MATCH |
| CLICINFO offset | 0x004 | 0x004 | MATCH |
| MINTTHRESH offset | 0x008 | 0x008 | MATCH |
| RESERVED[1021] | implied (gap to 0x1000) | RESERVED[1021] | MATCH |
| CLICINT[] start offset | 0x1000 | 0x1000 | MATCH |
| CLICINT entry count | comment says 4096 | CLICINT[4096] | MATCH |
| CLICINT[] element size | irq*4 (4 bytes per entry) | 4 x uint8_t = 4 bytes | MATCH |

**Per-entry byte offsets (IP/IE/ATTR/CTL): MATCHES**

The luban-lite CMSIS-style comments say offsets 0x000/0x004/0x008/0x00C for IP/IE/ATTR/CTL, but these are misleading comments in the reference header itself — the actual members are `uint8_t`, so the real packed byte offsets are +0/+1/+2/+3. The openvela code accesses them correctly:

- IP: `base + irq*4 + 0`
- IE: `base + irq*4 + 1`
- ATTR: `base + irq*4 + 2`

CTL (offset +3) is defined but not directly manipulated by any helper function — which matches luban-lite where CTL is also not written during init.

**DISCREPANCY 1 — CLIC_INT_Control offset comment in openvela:**
Lines 37-41 of `artinchip_irq.c` reproduce the same misleading offset comments from luban-lite:
```
 *   uint8_t IE;    // offset +0x004 (enable)
 *   uint8_t ATTR;  // offset +0x008 (attribute: vector/shv)
 *   uint8_t CTL;   // offset +0x00C (control: priority)
```
These are **not real byte offsets** — they are carried over from the luban-lite header. The actual offsets are +1, +2, +3. The code itself is correct (uses `+1`, `+2`), but the comments are misleading. This is a **documentation-only issue** inherited from the reference.

---

### 2. CLICCFG Initialization — `up_irqinitialize()` vs. `SystemInit()`

**OpenVela (artinchip_irq.c, lines 132-134):**
```c
uint32_t info = *clicinfo;
uint32_t nlbits = (info >> 21) & 0xF;
*cliccfg = (nlbits << 1) & 0x1E;
```

**Luban-lite (system.c, line 123):**
```c
CLIC->CLICCFG = (((CLIC->CLICINFO & CLIC_INFO_CLICINTCTLBITS_Msk)
                  >> CLIC_INFO_CLICINTCTLBITS_Pos) << CLIC_CLICCFG_NLBIT_Pos);
```

Where:
- `CLIC_INFO_CLICINTCTLBITS_Msk` = `0xFUL << 21`
- `CLIC_INFO_CLICINTCTLBITS_Pos` = 21
- `CLIC_CLICCFG_NLBIT_Pos` = 1

**Translation:** `nlbits = (info >> 21) & 0xF; CLICCFG = nlbits << 1;`

**DISCREPANCY 2 — CLICCFG mask:**
- OpenVela applies `& 0x1E` (masking to bits [4:1]) — the NLBIT field is 4 bits at position 1, so valid range is `0x2` through `0x1E`. The `& 0x1E` is correct but slightly more conservative than luban-lite, which does **no mask** after the shift. The luban-lite relies on the fact that `nlbits` is already masked to 4 bits. The openvela version is equivalent and actually more defensive. **Not a functional discrepancy.**

---

### 3. Interrupt Init Loop — `up_irqinitialize()` vs. `SystemInit()`

**OpenVela:**
```c
for (i = 0; i < 96; i++) {
    d13x_clic_clear_pending(i);
    d13x_clic_set_attr(i, 1);  /* use vector interrupt */
}
```

**Luban-lite:**
```c
for (i = 0; i < MAX_IRQn; i++) {
    CLIC->CLICINT[i].IP = 0;
    CLIC->CLICINT[i].ATTR = 1;
}
CLIC->CLICINT[Machine_Software_IRQn].ATTR = 0x3;
drv_irq_enable(Machine_Software_IRQn);
```

**DISCREPANCY 3 — Loop count hardcoded to 96:**
OpenVela uses the hardcoded constant `96`. Luban-lite uses `MAX_IRQn` which is defined per-chip. For D13x this may or may not be 96. If `MAX_IRQn` for D13x is different, interrupts would not all be initialized.

**DISCREPANCY 4 — Machine_Software_IRQn special handling MISSING:**
Luban-lite explicitly sets `CLIC->CLICINT[Machine_Software_IRQn].ATTR = 0x3` (positive edge-triggered + vector) and then calls `drv_irq_enable(Machine_Software_IRQn)`. This is critical for the T-Head `tspend` inter-processor interrupt mechanism. OpenVela's `up_irqinitialize()` does **not** set up `Machine_Software_IRQn` with ATTR=0x3 and does **not** enable it. This will break any tspend-based functionality.

**DISCREPANCY 5 — IE not cleared during init:**
OpenVela clears IP and sets ATTR in the init loop, but does **not** explicitly clear IE (interrupt enable). Luban-lite also does not explicitly clear IE in the loop, but the CLIC hardware default for IE after reset is typically 0, so this is likely equivalent. However, if IE is non-zero after reset on some silicon revisions, this could cause spurious interrupts.

---

### 4. mtvec/mtvt CSR Setup — `up_irqinitialize()` vs. `startup_gcc.S`

**OpenVela (artinchip_irq.c, lines 116-122):**
```c
uint32_t mtvec = (uint32_t)__trap_vec | 0x3;
__asm__ __volatile__("csrw mtvec, %0" :: "r"(mtvec));
uint32_t mtvt = (uint32_t)__trap_vec;
__asm__ __volatile__("csrw 0x7C0, %0" :: "r"(mtvt));
```

**Luban-lite (startup_gcc.S, lines 136-140):**
```asm
la      a0, Default_Handler
ori     a0, a0, 3
csrw    mtvec, a0
la      a0, __Vectors
csrw    mtvt, a0
```

**DISCREPANCY 6 — mtvec points to different locations:**
- OpenVela: mtvec = `__trap_vec | 0x3` (trap vector table, a NuttX construct)
- Luban-lite: mtvec = `Default_Handler | 0x3` (the default C handler, not the vector table)

These are fundamentally different approaches. Luban-lite uses `mtvec` as a **direct mode** fallback (mode=3 means ECLIC mode on T-Head), with `mtvt` pointing to the actual vector table `__Vectors`. OpenVela sets mtvec to `__trap_vec | 0x3` which is the NuttX trap entry point with mode bits set. The T-Head ECLIC mode (bits [1:0] = 11) means mtvec is only used for non-vectored interrupts, while mtvt handles vectored dispatch. The question is whether NuttX's `__trap_vec` serves the same role as luban-lite's `Default_Handler` as a non-vectored fallback — it likely does, but the naming difference means the vector table contents differ.

**DISCREPANCY 7 — mtvt points to different tables:**
- OpenVela: mtvt = `__trap_vec` (NuttX trap vector table)
- Luban-lite: mtvt = `__Vectors` (the explicit vector table defined in `startup_gcc.S` lines 15-118)

In luban-lite, `__Vectors` is a hand-crafted array of 100 function pointers (entries 0-99), with specific entries for PendSV_Handler (entry 3) and Default_IRQHandler (entry 7). OpenVela's `__trap_vec` is a NuttX-provided symbol whose layout is determined by NuttX's arch code, not by the vendor startup. This is an **architectural difference** in how the two systems organize their vector tables.

---

### 5. Boot Flow Sequence — `artinchip_start.c` `__start()` vs. expected order

**OpenVela `__start()` flow (lines 461-505):**
1. Clear BSS
2. Copy .data
3. Disable watchdog
4. Clock init
5. UART init
6. PSRAM init
7. Print boot char ('D')
8. `nx_start()`

**Expected order (as stated in the verification request):**
BSS clear -> data copy -> watchdog disable -> clock init -> UART init -> PSRAM init -> nx_start

**RESULT: MATCHES the expected order exactly.**

**DISCREPANCY 8 — No .data copy in luban-lite's non-QEMU path:**
Luban-lite's `startup_gcc.S` only copies `.data` in the `QEMU_RUN` path (lines 201-214). On real hardware, luban-lite presumably has the bootloader or XIP setup that makes .data already in place. The openvela code always copies .data regardless of boot mode, which is more conservative and correct for a general bootloader-to-NuttX handoff.

---

### 6. Bootloader `startup.S` vs. luban-lite `startup_gcc.S`

**OpenVela bootloader (d13x-bootloader/src/startup.S):**
1. Save BROM parameters (a0-a7, s0-s11, sp, ra)
2. Copy boot_arg (256 bytes)
3. Set stack pointer
4. Clear BSS
5. Call `main`
6. WFI hang

**Luban-lite (startup_gcc.S):**
1. Jump to `save_boot_params`
2. Set gp register
3. Set mtvec (Default_Handler | 3)
4. Set mtvt (__Vectors)
5. Set stack pointer
6. Enable icache, dcache
7. TCM init (if AIC_TCM_EN)
8. SRAM init (if AIC_SRAM1_EN)
9. PSRAM uncache config
10. Copy .data (QEMU only)
11. Clear BSS
12. Call SystemInit
13. Call entry/main

**DISCREPANCY 9 — Bootloader missing gp register setup:**
The openvela bootloader does not set the global pointer (`gp`) register. Luban-lite sets it early (`la gp, __global_pointer$`). This affects relaxation and PIC code generation — any code using GP-relative addressing will fault.

**DISCREPANCY 10 — Bootloader missing vector table / CSR setup:**
The openvElA bootloader does not set `mtvec` or `mtvt` at all. Any interrupt during bootloader execution will vector to whatever the BROM left in those CSRs, which may cause a crash.

**DISCREPANCY 11 — Bootloader missing icache/dcache enable:**
Luban-lite enables both caches early. The openvela bootloader does not. For XIP execution this would be a significant performance penalty.

**DISCREPANCY 12 — Bootloader missing TCM init:**
No TCM (Tightly Coupled Memory) initialization. If the D13x relies on TCM for fast execution, this is a functional gap.

**DISCREPANCY 13 — Bootloader does not call SystemInit:**
Luban-lite calls `SystemInit` which performs CLIC init, FPU enable, T-Head ISA extensions, cache enable, and timer setup. The openvela bootloader does none of this.

**DISCREPANCY 14 — Bootloader .data section not copied:**
Unlike the NuttX `__start()`, the bootloader `startup.S` does not copy `.data`. If the bootloader has initialized globals, they will contain garbage.

---

### 7. `system.c` Reference — what OpenVela's `artinchip_irq.c` is missing

Comparing `up_irqinitialize()` to luban-lite `SystemInit()`:

**DISCREPANCY 15 — Missing mstatus.FS (FPU) enable:**
```c
// luban-lite does:
mstatus |= (1 << 13);  // FS field enable
```
OpenVela does not set this. If FPU is used, first access will trap.

**DISCREPANCY 16 — Missing mxstatus.THEADISAEE enable:**
```c
// luban-lite does:
mxstatus |= (1 << 22);  // T-Head ISA extension enable
mxstatus |= (1 << 15);  // Memory Management enable
```
OpenVela does not touch `mxstatus`. This is critical for T-Head E907 extensions.

**DISCREPANCY 17 — Missing mexstatus.SPUSHEN/SPSWAPEN:**
```c
// luban-lite does:
mexstatus |= (1 << 16); // SPUSHEN
mexstatus |= (1 << 17); // SPSWAPEN
```
These T-Head extensions improve interrupt context save performance.

**DISCREPANCY 18 — Missing dcache/icache enable in SystemInit:**
Luban-lite calls `csi_dcache_enable()` and `csi_icache_enable()` from `SystemInit()`. OpenVela's `up_irqinitialize()` does not.

---

### Summary of All Discrepancies

| 1 | Low | Doc | CLIC_INT_Control offset comments are misleading (+0x004 etc. vs actual +1) |

### 5. Flash Memory Size Concern

---

### Summary of Findings

1. **Origins are consistent** -- SRAM at `0x30040000`, PSRAM at `0x40000000`, Flash at `0x60000000` across all real-hardware scripts.

Here is the complete verification report across all five files.

---

## CLIC Register Layout Verification

**Reference source:** luban-lite `core_rv32.h` lines 136-151 defines `CLIC_INT_Control` and `CLIC_Type`.

**Luban-lite struct layout:**
- CLICCFG at offset 0x000
- CLICINFO at offset 0x004
- MINTTHRESH at offset 0x008
- RESERVED[1021] filling the gap
- CLICINT[4096] starting at offset 0x1000

**Each CLICINT entry contains four packed uint8_t members:** IP (+0), IE (+1), ATTR (+2), CTL (+3), making each entry exactly 4 bytes.

**OpenVela `artinchip_irq.c` lines 28-41 comment block** replicates this layout. The base addresses (`CLIC_CFG = base+0x000`, `CLIC_INFO = base+0x004`, `CLIC_INT_BASE = base+0x1000`) are correct. The `irq*4` stride for indexing CLICINT entries is correct.

**One documentation issue (Discrepancy A):** The comment block at lines 38-41 states byte offsets `+0x004`, `+0x008`, `+0x00C` for the uint8_t members IE, ATTR, CTL respectively. These are copied verbatim from luban-lite's own misleading CMSIS-style Doxygen comments. The real byte offsets are +1, +2, +3. The actual register access code at lines 70, 78, 86, 94 uses the correct `+0`, `+1`, `+2` offsets. So the code works correctly despite the wrong-looking comments.

---

## CLICCFG Initialization Formula Verification

**Luban-lite `system.c` line 123:**
```
CLIC->CLICCFG = ((CLIC->CLICINFO & 0xF<<21) >> 21) << 1
```
This extracts bits [24:21] from CLICINFO (the `nlbits` field) and shifts left by 1 to place them at NLBIT position [4:1] in CLICCFG.

**OpenVela `artinchip_irq.c` lines 132-134:**
```
nlbits = (info >> 21) & 0xF;
*cliccfg = (nlbits << 1) & 0x1E;
```
Identical computation, with an extra `& 0x1E` guard that luban-lite omits. Since nlbits is already 4-bit, the mask is redundant but harmless. **No functional discrepancy.**

---

## CLIC Interrupt Init Loop Verification

**Luban-lite `system.c` lines 125-129** iterates `i = 0..MAX_IRQn-1`, clears IP to 0, and sets ATTR to 1 (vector mode).

**OpenVela `artinchip_irq.c` lines 138-142** iterates `i = 0..95`, clears IP and sets ATTR to 1.

**Discrepancy B -- Loop bound:** OpenVela hardcodes 96. Luban-lite uses `MAX_IRQn`, which is chip-specific. If D13x has more than 96 interrupt sources, some would not get initialized.

**Discrepancy C -- Missing Machine_Software_IRQn handling:** After the main loop, luban-lite at line 132 does:
```c
CLIC->CLICINT[Machine_Software_IRQn].ATTR = 0x3;
drv_irq_enable(Machine_Software_IRQn);
```
This configures the machine software interrupt as level+edge triggered (ATTR=0x3) and enables it, which is essential for T-Head's tspend mechanism. OpenVela performs neither of these steps.

---

## mtvec / mtvt CSR Setup Verification

**Luban-lite `startup_gcc.S` lines 136-140:**
```asm
la      a0, Default_Handler    ; load address of C default handler
ori     a0, a0, 3              ; set mode bits [1:0] = 11 (ECLIC mode)
csrw    mtvec, a0              ; mtvec = Default_Handler | 3
la      a0, __Vectors          ; load address of explicit vector table
csrw    mtvt, a0               ; mtvt = __Vectors
```

**OpenVela `artinchip_irq.c` lines 116-122:**
```c
mtvec = __trap_vec | 0x3;
csrw mtvec, mtvt
mtvt = __trap_vec;
csrw 0x7C0, mtvt
```

**Discrepancy D -- mtvec target differs:** Luban-lite points mtvec at a named C function (`Default_Handler`). OpenVela points it at a linker symbol (`__trap_vec`). These serve the same architectural role (non-vectored fallback under ECLIC mode 3), but the openvela symbol comes from NuttX's arch-level trap entry, not from a hand-built table. This is a design divergence but not necessarily wrong if NuttX's trap entry handles non-vectored dispatch correctly.

**Discrepancy E -- mtvt table differs:** Luban-lite's `__Vectors` is an explicit 100-entry table defined in `startup_gcc.S` lines 15-118 with specific named entries (PendSV_Handler at index 3, Default_IRQHandler at index 7). OpenVela's `__trap_vec` is a NuttX arch-provided symbol whose contents are defined elsewhere in the NuttX build. The vector table structure may be incompatible if NuttX expects a different entry layout than the Artinchip hardware interrupt numbering.

**Discrepancy F -- CSR write order:** Luban-lite writes mtvec first, then mtvt. OpenVela also writes mtvec first, then mtvt. Order matches. However, luban-lite does this during `Reset_Handler` (assembly startup), while openvela does it inside `up_irqinitialize()` (a C function called later). This means openvElA has a window between boot and IRQ init where interrupts could fire with stale CSR values.

---

## Boot Flow Sequence Verification

**OpenVela `__start()` (artinchip_start.c lines 461-505):**
1. BSS clear (lines 467-470)
2. .data copy (lines 474-477)
3. Watchdog disable via `d13x_watchdog_init()` (line 481)
4. Clock init via `d13x_clock_init()` (line 485)
5. UART init via `d13x_uart_init()` (line 489)
6. PSRAM init via `d13x_psram_init()` (line 493)
7. Print 'D' to UART (line 497)
8. `nx_start()` (line 501)

The requested verification order (BSS, data, watchdog, clock, UART, PSRAM, nx_start) is satisfied exactly. No discrepancy in ordering.

**Discrepancy G -- PSRAM init contains early-exit optimization:** `d13x_psram_init()` first calls `d13x_psram_verify()` which does a read/write test. If the test passes (bootloader already initialized PSRAM), it returns immediately. This is a reasonable optimization but not present in the luban-lite reference `SystemInit()`.

**Discrepancy H -- Clock register values are hardcoded magic numbers:** Lines 102, 110, 118, 119, 123, 134 use raw register values (e.g., `0x240C4040` for PLL config) without named bitfield constants. These should be verified against the D13x user manual or luban-lite HAL code to confirm correctness. The luban-lite reference uses HAL functions (`hal_clk_pll_lowpower()`, etc.) rather than raw register writes.

---

## Bootloader `startup.S` Verification

**OpenVela d13x-bootloader `startup.S` sequence:**
1. Save BROM arguments (a0-a7, s0-s11, sp, ra) -- lines 8-33
2. Copy boot_arg structure (256 bytes) -- lines 36-48
3. Set stack pointer -- lines 50-52
4. Clear BSS -- lines 54-62
5. Call `main` -- line 65
6. WFI hang -- lines 67-69

**Discrepancy I -- No data section copy:** Unlike `artinchip_start.c`, the bootloader does not copy `.data` from flash to RAM. Any initialized global variables will contain zeros (from BSS clearing) rather than their initial values.

**Discrepancy J -- No GP register initialization:** Luban-lite's `startup_gcc.S` line 134 does `la gp, __global_pointer$`. The bootloader omits this entirely. Global variable access via GP-relative addressing (the default for position-independent code) will produce wrong addresses or faults.

**Discrepancy K -- No mtvec/mtvt setup:** The bootloader leaves the trap CSRs at whatever the BROM configured. Any exception or interrupt during bootloader execution will vector to an unpredictable location.

**Discrepancy L -- No cache enable:** No icache or dcache configuration. For XIP execution from flash, this would cause severe performance degradation.

**Discrepancy M -- No TCM initialization:** The luban-lite startup configures itcm/dtcm via `mitcmcr`/`mdtcmcr` CSRs (lines 158-166 of startup_gcc.S). The bootloader skips this.

**Discrepancy N -- No SystemInit call:** The bootloader jumps directly to `main` without any hardware initialization beyond BSS clearing and stack setup.

**Discrepancy O -- No FPU/mxstatus/mexstatus CSR setup:** Luban-lite's `SystemInit()` enables FPU (mstatus.FS), T-Head ISA extensions (mxstatus bit 22), memory management (mxstatus bit 15), and stack push/swap optimization (mexstatus bits 16-17). The bootloader does none of this.

---

## Summary Table

| ID | Severity | File | Issue |
|----|----------|------|-------|
| A | Low | artinchip_irq.c | CLIC_INT_Control offset comments show +0x004/+0x008/+0x00C instead of +1/+2/+3; code itself is correct |
| B | Medium | artinchip_irq.c | CLIC init loop hardcoded to 96 iterations instead of using MAX_IRQn constant |
| C | **High** | artinchip_irq.c | Machine_Software_IRQn ATTR=0x3 setup and drv_irq_enable() call missing (breaks tspend IPC) |
| D | Low | artinchip_irq.c | mtvec points to NuttX `__trap_vec` rather than a named `Default_Handler`; functionally equivalent if NuttX handles non-vectored dispatch |
| E | Medium | artinchip_irq.c | mtvt points to NuttX arch symbol instead of a hand-built interrupt vector table; entry layout may differ from Artinchip hardware numbering |
| F | Medium | artinchip_irq.c | CSR setup deferred to C runtime (up_irqinitialize) rather than assembly startup; window where interrupts could fire with stale CSRs |
| G | Info | artinchip_start.c | PSRAM init has early-exit verify optimization not in luban-lite reference |
| H | Medium | artinchip_start.c | Clock configuration uses hardcoded magic numbers without bitfield definitions |
| I | Medium | startup.S | Bootloader does not copy .data section; initialized globals will be wrong |
| J | **High** | startup.S | GP register never initialized; breaks GP-relative addressing |
| K | High | startup.S | mtvec/mtvt CSRs left at BROM defaults; unpredictable exception behavior |
| L | Medium | startup.S | No cache enable; severe XIP performance penalty |
| M | Low | startup.S | No TCM init; fast execution path unavailable |
| N | Medium | startup.S | No SystemInit call; minimal hardware setup |
| O | High | startup.S | No FPU/T-Head ISA extension/mexstatus CSR setup; first FP or T-Head instruction will trap |

The three **high-severity** items (C, J, K, O) represent functional gaps that would cause runtime failures: missing tspend interrupt setup (C), broken global variable access in bootloader (J), unpredictable exception handling in bootloader (K), and instruction faults when T-Head extensions or FPU are used (O).

    .extern boot_params_stash

_start:
    /* 保存 BROM 传入的启动参数 (a0, a1) */

    la      t0, boot_params_stash
    sw      a0, 0(t0)       /* boot_device/boot_reason */
    sw      a1, 4(t0)       /* private_data address */

    /* 保存其余寄存器 */

    sw      a2, 8(t0)
    sw      a3, 12(t0)
    sw      a4, 16(t0)
    sw      a5, 20(t0)
    sw      a6, 24(t0)
    sw      a7, 28(t0)
    sw      s0, 32(t0)
    sw      s1, 36(t0)
    sw      s2, 40(t0)
    sw      s3, 44(t0)
    sw      s4, 48(t0)
    sw      s5, 52(t0)
    sw      s6, 56(t0)
    sw      s7, 60(t0)
    sw      s8, 64(t0)
    sw      s9, 68(t0)
    sw      s10, 72(t0)
    sw      s11, 76(t0)
    sw      sp, 80(t0)
    sw      ra, 84(t0)

    /* 拷贝 boot_arg (256 字节) */

    beqz    a1, .Lskip_boot_arg
    la      t0, boot_arg
    mv      t1, a1
    li      t2, 256
    add     t2, t1, t2
.Lcopy_boot_arg:
    bgeu    t1, t2, .Lskip_boot_arg
    lw      t3, (t1)
    sw      t3, (t0)
    addi    t0, t0, 4
    addi    t1, t1, 4
    j       .Lcopy_boot_arg
.Lskip_boot_arg:

    .option pop

    /* 初始化 GP 寄存器 (来源: luban-lite startup_gcc.S) */

    .option push
    .option norelax
    la      gp, __global_pointer$
    .option pop

    /* 设置栈指针 */

    la      sp, _estack
    andi    sp, sp, ~0x7

    la      t0, _sbss
    la      t1, _ebss

    addi    t0, t0, 4
    j       .Lclear_bss
.Lbss_done:

    j       .Lhang

    .align 4

+ ****************************************************************************/
+
+/* T-Head E907 扩展 CSR */
+
+#define CSR_MXSTATUS     0x7C0
+#define CSR_MEXSTATUS    0x7C1
+#define CSR_MSTATUS      0x300
+#define CSR_MTVEC        0x305
+#define CSR_MTVT         0x7C0

+/****************************************************************************
+ * SystemInit (来源: luban-lite system.c)
+ * 由 startup.S 在 BSS 清零后调用
+ ****************************************************************************/
+
+void SystemInit(void)
+{
+  /* 使能 mstatus FS (FPU) */
+
+  uint32_t mstatus;
+  __asm__ __volatile__("csrr %0, mstatus" : "=r"(mstatus));
+  mstatus |= (1 << 13);  /* FS = 01 (Initial) */
+  __asm__ __volatile__("csrw mstatus, %0" :: "r"(mstatus));
+
+  /* 使能 mxstatus THEADISAEE (T-Head ISA 扩展) */
+
+  uint32_t mxstatus;
+  __asm__ __volatile__("csrr %0, 0x7C0" : "=r"(mxstatus));
+  mxstatus |= (1 << 22);  /* THEADISAEE */
+  mxstatus |= (1 << 15);  /* MM (Memory Management) */
+  __asm__ __volatile__("csrw 0x7C0, %0" :: "r"(mxstatus));
+
+  /* 使能 mexstatus SPUSHEN/SPSWAPEN */
+
+  uint32_t mexstatus;
+  __asm__ __volatile__("csrr %0, 0x7C1" : "=r"(mexstatus));
+  mexstatus |= (1 << 16);  /* SPUSHEN */
+  mexstatus |= (1 << 17);  /* SPSWAPEN */
+  __asm__ __volatile__("csrw 0x7C1, %0" :: "r"(mexstatus));
+}
+
+/****************************************************************************
  * 寄存器访问宏
  ****************************************************************************/
 
 #define getreg32(a)     (*(volatile uint32_t *)(a))

The User Manual (Table 12-25, lines 96114-96302) defines these UART register offsets:

| Register | User Manual Offset | chip.h Offset | Match? |
|----------|-------------------|---------------|--------|
| RBR/THR/DLL | 0x000 | 0x00 (`UART_RBR_THR_DLL`) | CORRECT |
| DLH/IER | 0x004 | 0x04 (`UART_DLH`) | CORRECT |
| IIR/FCR | 0x008 | 0x08 (`UART_FCR`) | CORRECT |
| LCR | 0x00C | 0x0C (`UART_LCR`) | CORRECT |
| MCR | 0x010 | 0x10 (`UART_MCR`) | CORRECT |
| LSR | 0x014 | 0x14 (`UART_LSR`) | CORRECT |
| MSR | 0x018 | 0x18 (`UART_MSR`) | CORRECT |

**No missing offsets found.** All seven register offsets in chip.h match the User Manual exactly.

---

### 2. Missing Register Definitions in chip.h

The chip.h is missing several registers that the reference HAL code (`aic_hal_uart.c`) uses and the User Manual documents:

| Missing Register | Offset | Used By HAL? | Severity |
|-----------------|--------|-------------|----------|
| `UART_USR` | 0x7C | Yes (busy check) | **HIGH** |
| `UART_HALT` | 0xA4 | Yes (baudrate config) | **MEDIUM** |
| `UART_SCH` | 0x1C | No | Low |

---

### 3. ISSUE #1 (CRITICAL): DLAB/Divisor Setup is Wrong in `d13x_uart_setup()`

**File:** `artinchip_uart.c`, lines 44-58

The code writes LCR=0 first, then attempts to write DLL and DLH. But the User Manual (line 96062-96066) is unambiguous:

> "If DLAB is 0, offset 0x00 is TX/RX FIFO, offset 0x04 is IER register."
> "If DLAB is 1, offset 0x00 is DLL, offset 0x04 is DLH."

The current sequence:
```
putreg32(0, ... + UART_LCR);                    // LCR=0 → DLAB=0
putreg32(divisor & 0xFF, ... + UART_RBR_THR_DLL); // writing THR, NOT DLL!
putreg32((divisor >> 8) & 0xFF, ... + UART_DLH);  // writing IER, NOT DLH!
putreg32(0x03, ... + UART_LCR);                   // 8N1, but divisor never set
```

With DLAB=0, offset 0x00 maps to THR (write) and offset 0x04 maps to IER. The divisor values are written to the wrong registers entirely. The baud rate divisor is never actually programmed.

**Correct sequence** (as demonstrated by the reference HAL at `aic_hal_uart.c` lines 149-159):
```
putreg32(LCR_DLAB, ... + UART_LCR);    // LCR[7]=1 → DLAB=1
putreg32(divisor & 0xFF, ... + UART_RBR_THR_DLL);  // NOW writing DLL
putreg32((divisor >> 8) & 0xFF, ... + UART_DLH);   // NOW writing DLH
putreg32(0x03, ... + UART_LCR);         // Set 8N1, clear DLAB
```

---

### 4. ISSUE #2 (HIGH): No USR Busy Check Before Register Writes

The User Manual explicitly requires checking `USR[0]` (BUSY) before writing LCR and divisor registers. Five separate LCR bit descriptions (lines 97116, 97164, 97183, 97196, 97212) state:

> "仅当 UART 空闲时（USR[0] 为 0）此位才可写" (This bit can only be written when UART is idle, USR[0]=0)

And for DLL/DLH (lines 96512-96513, 96564-96565):

> "仅当 DLAB 位 (LCR[7]) 为 1 并且 UART 空闲 (USR[0]) 时，该寄存器才能被访问"

The reference HAL (`aic_hal_uart.c` line 31) has the `WAIT_USART_IDLE` macro that polls `addr->USR & USR_UART_BUSY` with a timeout before any register configuration. The NuttX driver in `d13x_uart_setup()` performs zero USR checks.

Additionally, `UART_USR` is not even defined in `chip.h`, so the driver has no way to perform this check.

---

### 5. ISSUE #3 (MEDIUM): RX Interrupt Enable Logic Uses Wrong Register Offset

**File:** `artinchip_uart.c`, lines 91-107

The `d13x_uart_rxint()` function reads and writes `UART_DLH` (offset 0x04) to manipulate interrupt enable bits. This works *only* when DLAB=0, because with DLAB=0, offset 0x04 maps to IER. However:

- There is no code ensuring DLAB=0 before accessing this register.
- After `d13x_uart_setup()` sets LCR=0x03 (which clears DLAB), the function should work correctly **if** the setup had been done properly. But there is no guard.
- The HAL code (`aic_hal_uart.c` lines 343-361) manipulates IER directly via `addr->IER |= flag` / `addr->IER &= ~flag`, which is a struct-based access that is DLAB-independent.

The bit masks are correct per the User Manual:
- `IER[0]` = ERBFI (RX Data Available Interrupt Enable) -- the code uses `0x01` which matches.
- `IER[1]` = ETBEI (TX Holding Register Empty Interrupt Enable) -- not defined in chip.h.

---

### 6. ISSUE #4 (MEDIUM): `d13x_uart_send()` Waits for THRE but Does Not Check USR Before Writing THR

**File:** `artinchip_uart.c`, lines 114-118

The send function polls `UART_LSR & UART_LSR_THRE` before writing THR. This is the standard 16550 pattern and is correct per the User Manual (line 96474): "串行输出端口发送的数据，仅当线路状态寄存器 (LSR) 中的 THRE 位 (LSR[5]) 被设为 1 时，数据才会写到该寄存器。"

However, the reference HAL (`aic_hal_uart.c` lines 459, 476) additionally checks `addr->USR & USR_UART_BUSY` before writing THR, with a comment "fix hardware bug." This suggests there may be a D13x hardware errata where THRE alone is insufficient. The NuttX driver omits this workaround.

---

### 7. ISSUE #5 (MEDIUM): `d13x_uart_lowputc()` Same USR Missing

**File:** `artinchip_lowputc.c`, lines 29-38

The low-level put character function polls THRE then writes THR directly, without any USR busy check. Same hardware bug concern as issue #4.

### 8. ISSUE #6 (LOW): `d13x_uart_attach()` Enables IRQ Without Disabling IER First

**File:** `artinchip_uart.c`, lines 64-72

The `d13x_uart_attach()` function calls `irq_attach()` and `up_enable_irq()` but never disables stale interrupts via IER before enabling the IRQ line. If there are pending interrupt conditions, this could cause an immediate spurious interrupt. The reference HAL (`aic_hal_uart.c` line 715) zeroes IER (`addr->IER = 0`) during initialization before attaching the handler.

---

### 9. ISSUE #7 (LOW): `d13x_uart_handler()` Reads Into Local Variable and Discards

**File:** `artinchip_uart.c`, lines 29-35

The ISR reads RBR into `volatile uint32_t thr` and then casts it to void. The comment says "读取字符并放入缓冲区" (read character and put into buffer) but the data is never passed to `uart_recvchars()`. The received data is silently lost.

The call `uart_register("/dev/console", &g_d13x_uart0)` matches the NuttX API signature at `nuttx/include/nuttx/serial/serial.h` line 430: `int uart_register(FAR const char *path, FAR uart_dev_t *dev)`. The `g_d13x_uart0` variable is declared as `uart_dev_t` at line 157. This is correct.

# PSRAM Initialization Verification Report

## Files Analyzed

1. `/home/lladlam/OpenVela/openvela/vendor/artinchip/chips/d13x/artinchip_start.c` (OpenVela NuttX startup)
2. `/home/lladlam/OpenVela/d13x-bootloader/src/system.c` (OpenVela bootloader)
3. `/home/lladlam/OpenVela/luban-lite/bsp/artinchip/hal/xspi/xspi_hw_v1.0.h` (luban-lite HAL header)
4. `/home/lladlam/OpenVela/luban-lite/bsp/artinchip/drv_bare/psram/xspi_psram.c` (luban-lite PSRAM driver)
5. `/home/lladlam/OpenVela/luban-lite/bsp/artinchip/hal/xspi/hal_xspi.c` (luban-lite XSPI HAL)
6. `/tmp/d13x_user_manual.txt` (D13x User Manual)

---

## DISCREPANCY 1 (CRITICAL): XSPI Register Map Is Entirely Wrong in OpenVela

The OpenVela code defines a fabricated register layout at offsets 0x100-0x118 that has **no correspondence** to actual hardware registers.

**Official D13x User Manual (Table 9-15) and luban-lite HAL register map:**

| Offset | Manual Name | luban-lite HAL Name | Function |
|--------|------------|---------------------|----------|
| 0x000 | XSPI_CTL | XSPI_REG_CTL | Control |
| 0x004 | XSPI_CLK | XSPI_REG_CLK | Clock divider |
| 0x008 | XSPI_TCR | XSPI_REG_TCR | Transmit control |
| 0x00C | XSPI_STAS | XSPI_REG_STAS | Status |
| 0x010 | XSPI_CS0_CTL | XSPI_REG_CSO_CTL | CS0 control |
| 0x014 | XSPI_CS0_DCTL | XSPI_REG_CS0_DCTL | CS0 DLL control |
| 0x018 | XSPI_CS1_CTL | XSPI_REG_CS1_CTL | CS1 control |
| 0x01C | XSPI_CS1_DCTL | XSPI_REG_CS1_DCTL | CS1 DLL control |
| 0x020 | XSPI_IER | XSPI_REG_IER | Interrupt enable |
| 0x024 | XSPI_ISR | XSPI_REG_ISR | Interrupt status |
| 0x028 | XSPI_FCR | XSPI_REG_FCR | FIFO control |
| 0x02C | XSPI_FSR | XSPI_REG_FSR | FIFO status |
| 0x030 | XSPI_START | XSPI_REG_START | LUT start trigger |
| 0x034 | XSPI_ADDR | XSPI_REG_ADDR | Address config |
| 0x038 | XSPI_FMR | XSPI_REG_FMR | Format config |
| 0x040 | XSPI_BTR | XSPI_REG_BTR | Burst type |
| 0x044 | XSPI_RCC | XSPI_REG_RCC | Read cmd control |
| 0x048 | XSPI_NDMA_MODE_CTL | XSPI_REG_NDMA_MODE_CTL | DMA mode |
| 0x050 | XSPI_TO | XSPI_REG_TO | Timeout |
| 0x054 | XSPI_LCKCR | XSPI_REG_LCKCR | LUT lock |
| 0x058 | XSPI_LUT_UP | XSPI_REG_LUT_UP | LUT update |
| 0x060 | XSPI_CS0_SEQUENCE | XSPI_REG_CS0_SEQUENCE | CS0 sequence |
| 0x064 | XSPI_CS1_SEQUENCE | XSPI_REG_CS1_SEQUENCE | CS1 sequence |
| 0x068 | XSPI_IO_CTL | XSPI_REG_IO_CTL | IO control |
| 0x100 | XSPI_LUTn (base) | XSPI_REG_LUTN | Look-Up Table entries |
| 0x200 | XSPI_TDR | XSPI_REG_TDR | TX data register |
| 0x300 | XSPI_RDR | XSPI_REG_RDR | RX data register |
| 0xFFC | VERSION | XSPI_REG_VERSION | Version |

**OpenVela code (both files) defines:**

| Offset | OpenVela Name | Actual Hardware |
|--------|--------------|-----------------|
| 0x000 | XSPI_CFG | XSPI_CTL |
| 0x004 | XSPI_TIMING | XSPI_CLK |
| 0x008 | XSPI_CFG2 | XSPI_TCR |
| 0x100 | XSPI_CMD | **XSPI_LUTn[0]** -- NOT a CMD register! |
| 0x104 | XSPI_ADDR | **XSPI_LUTn[1]** -- NOT an ADDR register! |
| 0x108 | XSPI_DATA | **XSPI_LUTn[2]** -- NOT a DATA register! |
| 0x10C | XSPI_CFG3 | **XSPI_LUTn[3]** -- NOT a CFG3 register! |
| 0x110 | XSPI_STATUS | **XSPI_LUTn[4]** -- NOT a STATUS register! |
| 0x114 | XSPI_CTRL | **XSPI_LUTn[5]** -- NOT a CTRL trigger! |
| 0x118 | XSPI_BCNT | **XSPI_LUTn[6]** -- NOT a byte count register! |

The OpenVela code treats the XSPI as a simple command FIFO controller. The real XSPI is a **LUT-based** controller -- you program command sequences into look-up table entries, then trigger them. There are no "CMD", "DATA", "BCNT", "STATUS", or "CTRL" registers at offsets 0x100-0x118.

---

## DISCREPANCY 2 (CRITICAL): XSPI Status Register Bit Interpretation Is Wrong

**Manual (XSPI_STAS at 0x000C):**
- Bit 0: `XSPI_BUSY` -- set when a transfer is in progress
- Bit 1: `AXI_TRANS` -- set when AXI channel is transferring
- Bit 2: `AHB_TRANS` -- set when AHB channel is transferring

**OpenVela code:**
```c
#define XSPI_STATUS_BUSY    (1 << 0)   // Correct -- maps to XSPI_BUSY
#define XSPI_STATUS_DONE    (1 << 1)   // WRONG -- bit 1 is AXI_TRANS, NOT "DONE"
```

The `d13x_xspi_wait_done()` function polls bit 1 as a "DONE" flag, but bit 1 is actually `AXI_TRANS`. There is **no "DONE" bit** in XSPI_STAS. The luban-lite code polls bit 0 (BUSY) going low to detect completion, which is the correct approach:
```c
static inline u8 xspi_hw_check_idle_status(u32 base)
{
    return (readl(XSPI_REG_STAS(base)) & STAS_BIT_BUSY_MSK);  // bit 0 only
}
```

---

## DISCREPANCY 3 (CRITICAL): XSPI Control Register Bit Definitions Are Wrong

**Manual (XSPI_CTL at 0x000):**
- Bit 0: `XSPI_EN` -- module enable
- Bit 1: `IDL_LOW_POWER_EN` -- idle low power
- Bit 2: `XIP_EN` -- XIP mode enable
- Bit 3: `AXI_WRAP_BURST_CTL`
- Bits 4-5: `XSPI_MODE_SEL` (0=Xccela, 1=Hyperbus, 2=OPI, 3=SPI)
- Bit 6: `PARALLEL_MODE`
- Bit 7: `TIMEOUT_EN`
- Bit 8: `Reset_level` (default=1)
- Bit 9: `Reset_en`

**OpenVela code defines:**
```c
#define XSPI_CFG_EN         (1 << 0)   // Maps to XSPI_EN -- correct
#define XSPI_CFG_RST        (1 << 1)   // WRONG -- bit 1 is IDL_LOW_POWER_EN, not reset
#define XSPI_CFG_CLK_EN     (1 << 2)   // WRONG -- bit 2 is XIP_EN, not clock enable
```

The `d13x_xspi_init()` function does:
```c
putreg32(XSPI_CFG_RST, XSPI_CFG);    // Writes 0x02 (IDL_LOW_POWER_EN=1) expecting reset
while (getreg32(XSPI_CFG) & XSPI_CFG_RST);  // Polls bit 1 -- will hang or false-pass
```

The real XSPI has no software reset bit in XSPI_CTL. The official code resets by calling `xspi_hw_reset()` which writes 0 to XSPI_CTL.

---

## DISCREPANCY 4 (CRITICAL): XIP Enable Uses Wrong Bits

**luban-lite code (`xspi_hw_set_xip_en`):**
```c
val |= CTL_BIT_XIP_EN_VAL(en);  // Sets bit 2 (XIP_EN)
```

**OpenVela code (`d13x_psram_xip_enable`):**
```c
cfg |= (1 << 8);  // Comment says "XIP mode" but bit 8 is Reset_level!
cfg |= (1 << 9);  // Comment says "DDR mode" but bit 9 is Reset_en!
```

This writes to the Reset_level and Reset_en bits instead of XIP_EN (bit 2). The XIP mode will never actually be enabled, and the PSRAM device will not be memory-mapped.

---

## DISCREPANCY 5 (CRITICAL): Wrong CMU Clock Register for XSPI

**User Manual:**
- `CLK_XSPI` at CMU_BASE + **0x45C** (XSPI clock)
- `CLK_QSPI0` at CMU_BASE + **0x460** (QSPI0 clock, for SPI Flash)

**OpenVela PSRAM init code (both files):**
```c
/* 1. 使能 XSPI 时钟 (CMU_BASE + 0x460) */
uint32_t reg = getreg32(CMU_BASE + 0x460);  // WRONG -- this is CLK_QSPI0!
reg |= (1 << 13) | (1 << 12) | (1 << 8);
putreg32(reg, CMU_BASE + 0x460);
```

The comment says "enable XSPI clock" but the code writes to **0x460 (CLK_QSPI0)** instead of **0x45C (CLK_XSPI)**. This enables the QSPI0 (SPI Flash) clock module instead of the XSPI (PSRAM) clock module. The XSPI controller will have no clock and will not function.

---

## DISCREPANCY 6 (MAJOR): XSPI Protocol Mode Not Configured

**luban-lite init sequence (`hal_xspi_init`):**
```c
xspi_hw_set_xspi_mode(base, opi);  // Set XSPI_CTL[5:4] = 2 (OPI mode)
xspi_hw_set_clk_div(base, 0, 0);   // Configure clock divider
xspi_hw_set_cs_write_hold(base, 8); // Configure TCR write hold
xspi_hw_set_cs_read_hold(base, 2);  // Configure TCR read hold
xspi_hw_set_wrap_burst_split(base, 1); // Enable wrap burst split
xspi_hw_set_boudary_ctl(base, xspi_1k); // Set boundary control
xspi_hw_set_cs_iocfg(base, cs0, 0x36363636, 0x36363636, 0x36363636, 0x37);
xspi_hw_set_dll_ctl(base, cs0, ICP_150_200M, xspi_d_90b); // DLL config
xspi_hw_set_xspi_en(base, 1); // Enable XSPI module
```

**OpenVela init sequence:** None of these steps are performed. The OpenVela code:
- Does not set the XSPI protocol mode (Xccela/OPI/SPI)
- Does not configure clock dividers (XSPI_CLK)
- Does not configure CS write/read hold (XSPI_TCR)
- Does not configure IO drive strength (IOCFG registers)
- Does not configure DLL settings (CS0_DCTL / CS1_DCTL)
- Does not enable wrap burst split

---

## DISCREPANCY 7 (MAJOR): XIP Protocol Configuration Is Missing

**luban-lite XIP setup (`aic_xspi_psram_xip`):**
The official code configures a full protocol descriptor for XIP:
```c
psram_proto_cfg.mode = XSPI_MODE_OPI;
psram_proto_cfg.clk_mode = XSPI_DDR_MODE;
psram_proto_cfg.wr_cmd_val = 0x80;      // write command
psram_proto_cfg.rd_cmd_val = 0x00;       // read command
psram_proto_cfg.addr_width = 3;          // 3-byte address
psram_proto_cfg.wr_dummy = 2;            // write dummy cycles
psram_proto_cfg.rd_dummy = 0x06;         // read dummy cycles
psram_proto_cfg.wr_cnt = 2;              // write burst count
psram_proto_cfg.rd_cnt = 3;              // read burst count
```
This configures **LUT entries 0-3 for write** and **LUT entries 16-19 for read**, using the proper DDR/OPI protocol format. Then calls `xspi_hw_lut_update()` and `xspi_hw_lut_lock_ctl(LUT_LOCK)`.

**OpenVela XIP setup:**
```c
putreg32(0x00000000, XSPI_CFG2);  // "XIP base address" -- wrong register
putreg32(0x00000000, XSPI_CFG3);  // "XIP size" -- wrong register
```
This writes zeros to LUT entries 1 and 2 (not "CFG2" and "CFG3"), which corrupts the LUT table. No protocol configuration, no read/write LUT entries, no LUT update, no LUT lock.

---

## DISCREPANCY 8 (MAJOR): No DLL/Training Phase

**luban-lite init includes DLL training:**
```c
xspi_hw_set_dll_ctl(base, cs0, ICP_150_200M, xspi_d_90b);
xspi_hw_set_dll_ctl(base, cs1, ICP_150_200M, xspi_d_90b);
// ... then after XIP enable:
aic_xspi_psram_training(&handle, 0, icp_t, psram_buf, len);  // CS0
aic_xspi_psram_training(&handle, 1, icp_t, psram_buf, len);  // CS1
```
Training iterates over DLL phase selections (0-14) to find the optimal sampling point, using memory test patterns.

**OpenVela:** No DLL configuration and no training phase. PSRAM access may fail at higher clock rates without proper DLL calibration.

---

## DISCREPANCY 9 (MAJOR): Missing CS1 Initialization

**luban-lite init:**
```c
hal_xspi_set_cs(&handle, 0);
aic_xspi_psram_dev_reset(&handle);
aic_udelay(100);
aic_xspi_psram_dev_init(&handle);

hal_xspi_set_cs(&handle, 1);  // Also initialize CS1
aic_xspi_psram_dev_reset(&handle);
aic_udelay(100);
aic_xspi_psram_dev_init(&handle);
```

**OpenVela:** Only initializes CS0. CS1 is never configured. If a second PSRAM chip is present, it will not be initialized.

---

## DISCREPANCY 10 (MODERATE): No Delay After PSRAM Reset

**luban-lite:** `aic_udelay(100)` after device reset.
**OpenVela:** No delay between reset command and device init. PSRAM devices require time after reset to complete internal initialization. Skipping the delay can cause mode register writes to fail.

---

## DISCREPANCY 11 (MODERATE): Missing XSPI Mode Selection for PSRAM Commands

The luban-lite PSRAM commands (reset, read MR, write MR) use LUT-based transfers via `hal_xspi_transfer_cpu_sync()`. The OpenVela code attempts to use direct register writes at fabricated offsets. Even if the register offsets were correct, the XSPI controller requires LUT configuration before any AHB command can be executed.

---

## DISCREPANCY 12 (MINOR): Both OpenVela Files Are Internally Consistent

The artinchip_start.c and d13x-bootloader system.c files define identical (equally wrong) XSPI register layouts and identical PSRAM init sequences. The discrepancies between these two files are:

1. **system.c** defines two additional registers: `XSPI_ACNT` (0x11C) and `XSPI_DMA` (0x200). artinchip_start.c does not.
2. **system.c** defines two additional PSRAM commands: `PSRAM_CMD_WRITE` (0x80) and `PSRAM_CMD_READ` (0x00). artinchip_start.c does not.
3. **system.c** defines additional mode registers: `PSRAM_MR1` (0x01) and `PSRAM_MR2` (0x02). artinchip_start.c does not.
4. **system.c** has PSRAM chip ID defines. artinchip_start.c does not.

These additional definitions in system.c are closer to what would be needed, but the register offsets remain wrong.

---

## Summary of Discrepancies by Severity

### CRITICAL (will cause boot failure or incorrect hardware behavior):
1. **XSPI register map is fabricated** -- offsets 0x100-0x118 are LUT registers, not CMD/DATA/STATUS/CTRL
2. **Status register bit 1 is "AXI_TRANS", not "DONE"** -- polling will never detect completion correctly
3. **Control register bit definitions wrong** -- bit 1 is IDL_LOW_POWER_EN (not RST), bit 2 is XIP_EN (not CLK_EN)
4. **XIP enable uses bits 8/9 instead of bit 2** -- XIP will never be enabled; Reset_level/Reset_en will be clobbered
5. **Wrong CMU clock register** -- 0x460 (CLK_QSPI0) is used instead of 0x45C (CLK_XSPI); XSPI gets no clock

### MAJOR (init will complete but PSRAM will not function correctly):
6. **No protocol mode configuration** -- XSPI_MODE_SEL never set; controller defaults to Xccela mode (0) which may not match PSRAM
7. **No XIP LUT configuration** -- write/read LUT entries never programmed; memory-mapped access will send garbage
8. **No DLL training** -- no DLL configuration or phase training; access unreliable at any non-trivial clock speed
9. **No CS1 initialization** -- dual-die PSRAM configurations will fail

### MODERATE:
10. **No delay after PSRAM reset** -- timing violation
11. **No proper AHB/XIP transfer mechanism** -- direct register writes to LUT space will corrupt the look-up table
12. **Missing features in artinchip_start.c** (minor, both files equally broken for the same root cause)

---

## Verdict

The OpenVela PSRAM initialization code in both `artinchip_start.c` and `system.c` was written against an **invented register interface** that does not correspond to the actual D13x XSPI hardware. The XSPI controller is a LUT-based design (similar to FlexSPI/NXP i.MX), not a simple command-FIFO controller. Every stage of the PSRAM init -- clock enable, controller reset, command execution, status polling, and XIP setup -- targets wrong register offsets or wrong bit positions. **None of these functions would work on real hardware.** The code must be rewritten to use the LUT-based interface as implemented in the luban-lite HAL (`xspi_hw_v1.0.h` + `hal_xspi.c` + `xspi_psram.c`).
</actor_result>

181: #define XSPI_STATUS         (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x110)
182: #define XSPI_CTRL           (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x114)
183: #define XSPI_BCNT           (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x118)
184: 
185: /* XSPI 配置位 */
186: 
187: #define XSPI_CFG_EN         (1 << 0)
188: #define XSPI_CFG_RST        (1 << 1)
189: #define XSPI_CFG_CLK_EN     (1 << 2)

191: /* XSPI 状态位 */
192: 
193: #define XSPI_STATUS_BUSY    (1 << 0)
194: #define XSPI_STATUS_DONE    (1 << 1)

198: #define PSRAM_CMD_RESET     0xFF
199: #define PSRAM_CMD_READ_ID   0x40

201: #define PSRAM_CMD_READ_MR   0x40

208: static uint32_t d13x_psram_read_efuse(uint32_t reg_addr)
209: {
210:   /* 使能 eFuse 时钟 */
211: 
212:   putreg32(0x1100, EFUSE_CMU_REG);
213: 
214:   /* 读取 eFuse 值 */
215: 
216:   uint32_t val = getreg32(reg_addr);
217: 
218:   /* 关闭 eFuse 时钟 */
219: 
220:   putreg32(0x0, EFUSE_CMU_REG);
221: 
222:   return val;

225: static uint32_t d13x_psram_get_size(void)
226: {
227:   uint32_t fuse_218 = d13x_psram_read_efuse(EFUSE_218_REG);
228:   uint8_t mark_id = fuse_218 & 0xFF;
229: 
230:   /* 根据 mark_id 确定 PSRAM 大小 */
231: 
232:   switch (mark_id)
233:     {
234:       case 0x00:  /* force use cfg0 */
235:         return 0;
236:       case 0x01:  /* D131BAS 4M */
237:         return 4 * 1024 * 1024;
238:       case 0x02:  /* D131BBS 8M */
239:       case 0x03:  /* D131CBS 8M */
240:       case 0x04:  /* D131EBS/D133EBS 8M */
241:       case 0x05:  /* D132ENS 8M */
242:       case 0xA1:  /* DR128 8M */
243:       case 0xA2:  /* JYX68 8M */
244:         return 8 * 1024 * 1024;
245:       case 0x06:  /* D131CCS 16M */
246:       case 0x07:  /* D133ECS 16M */
247:         return 16 * 1024 * 1024;
248:       default:
249:         return 8 * 1024 * 1024;  /* 默认 8MB */
250:     }

254: {
255:   while (!(getreg32(XSPI_STATUS) & XSPI_STATUS_DONE));

258: static void d13x_psram_xspi_write_cmd(uint32_t cmd, uint32_t addr,
259:                                        uint8_t *data, int len)

261:   /* 等待空闲 */
262: 
263:   while (getreg32(XSPI_STATUS) & XSPI_STATUS_BUSY);
264: 
265:   /* 配置命令 */
266: 
267:   putreg32(cmd, XSPI_CMD);
268:   putreg32(addr, XSPI_ADDR);
269:   putreg32(len, XSPI_BCNT);

271:   /* 写入数据 */
272: 
273:   int i;
274:   for (i = 0; i < len; i++)
275:     {
276:       putreg32(data[i], XSPI_DATA);
277:     }
278: 
279:   /* 启动传输 */
280: 
281:   putreg32(1, XSPI_CTRL);
282: 
283:   /* 等待完成 */
284: 
285:   d13x_xspi_wait_done();

305:   /* 等待完成 */

357:   putreg32(0x00000000, XSPI_CFG3);  /* XIP 大小 */

368:   /* 写入测试模式 */
369: 
370:   psram[0] = 0x12345678;
371:   psram[1] = 0x9ABCDEF0;
372: 
373:   /* 读取并验证 */
374: 
375:   if (psram[0] != 0x12345678)
376:     return 0;
377: 
378:   if (psram[1] != 0x9ABCDEF0)
379:     return 0;
380: 
381:   /* 清除测试数据 */
382: 
383:   psram[0] = 0;
384:   psram[1] = 0;

386:   return psram_size;

393:   uint32_t psram_size = d13x_psram_verify();

395:   if (psram_size > 0)

398:       return;
399:     }

401:   /* PSRAM 未初始化，执行完整初始化 */
402: 
403:   /* 1. 使能 XSPI 时钟 (CMU_BASE + 0x460) */
404: 
405:   uint32_t reg = getreg32(D13X_CMU_BASE + 0x460);
406:   reg |= (1 << 13) | (1 << 12) | (1 << 8);
407:   putreg32(reg, D13X_CMU_BASE + 0x460);
408: 
409:   /* 2. 复位 XSPI 控制器 */
410: 
411:   putreg32(XSPI_CFG_RST, XSPI_CFG);
412:   while (getreg32(XSPI_CFG) & XSPI_CFG_RST);
413: 
414:   /* 3. 使能 XSPI 控制器 */
415: 
416:   putreg32(XSPI_CFG_EN | XSPI_CFG_CLK_EN, XSPI_CFG);
417: 
418:   /* 4. 复位 PSRAM 设备 */
419: 
420:   d13x_psram_device_reset();
421: 
422:   /* 5. 配置 PSRAM 设备 */
423: 
424:   d13x_psram_device_init();
425: 
426:   /* 6. 使能 XIP 模式 */
427: 
428:   d13x_psram_xip_enable();
429: 
430:   /* 7. 验证初始化 */
431: 
432:   d13x_psram_verify();
433: }

131:   \param[in]   addr  usart base to operate.
132:   \return      error code
133: */
134: int32_t hal_usart_config_baudrate(usart_handle_t handle, uint32_t baud)
135: {
136:     USART_NULL_PARAM_CHK(handle);
137:     aic_usart_priv_t *usart_priv = handle;
138:     aic_usart_reg_t *addr = (aic_usart_reg_t *)(usart_priv->base);
139: 
140:     /* baudrate=(seriak clock freq)/(16*divisor); algorithm :rounding*/
141:     uint32_t divisor = ((hal_clk_get_freq(CLK_UART0 + usart_priv->idx)  * 10) / baud) >> 4;
142: 
143:     if ((divisor % 10) >= 5) {
144:         divisor = (divisor / 10) + 1;
145:     } else {
146:         divisor = divisor / 10;
147:     }
148: 
149:     addr->HALT |= (HALT_CHCFG_AT_BUSY);
150: 
151:     addr->LCR |= LCR_SET_DLAB;
152:     /* DLL and DLH is lower 8-bits and higher 8-bits of divisor.*/
153:     addr->DLL = divisor & 0xff;
154:     addr->DLH = (divisor >> 8) & 0xff;
155:     /*
156:      * The DLAB must be cleared after the baudrate is setted
157:      * to access other registers.
158:      */
159:     addr->LCR &= (~LCR_SET_DLAB);
160: 
161:     addr->HALT |= (HALT_CHANGE_UPDATE);
162: 
163:     return 0;
164: }

184: /**
185:   \brief       config usart parity.
186:   \param[in]   handle  usart handle to operate.
187:   \param[in]   parity    \ref usart_parity_e
188:   \return      error code
189: */
190: int32_t hal_usart_config_parity(usart_handle_t handle, usart_parity_e parity)
191: {
192:     USART_NULL_PARAM_CHK(handle);
193:     aic_usart_priv_t *usart_priv = handle;
194:     aic_usart_reg_t *addr = (aic_usart_reg_t *)(usart_priv->base);
195: 
196:     switch (parity)
197:     {
198:         case USART_PARITY_NONE:
199:             /*CLear the PEN bit(LCR[3]) to disable parity.*/
200:             addr->LCR &= (~LCR_PARITY_ENABLE);
201:             break;
202: 
203:         case USART_PARITY_ODD:
204:             /* Set PEN and clear EPS(LCR[4]) to set the ODD parity. */
205:             addr->LCR |= LCR_PARITY_ENABLE;
206:             addr->LCR &= LCR_PARITY_ODD;
207:             break;
208: 
209:         case USART_PARITY_EVEN:
210:             /* Set PEN and EPS(LCR[4]) to set the EVEN parity.*/
211:             addr->LCR |= LCR_PARITY_ENABLE;
212:             addr->LCR |= LCR_PARITY_EVEN;
213:             break;
214: 
215:         default:
216:             return ERR_USART(USART_ERROR_PARITY);
217:     }
218: 
219:     return 0;
220: }

222: /**
223:   \brief       config usart stop bit number.
224:   \param[in]   handle  usart handle to operate.
225:   \param[in]   stopbits  \ref usart_stop_bits_e
226:   \return      error code
227: */
228: int32_t hal_usart_config_stopbits(usart_handle_t handle, usart_stop_bits_e stopbit)
229: {
230:     USART_NULL_PARAM_CHK(handle);
231:     aic_usart_priv_t *usart_priv = handle;
232:     aic_usart_reg_t *addr = (aic_usart_reg_t *)(usart_priv->base);
233: 
234:     switch (stopbit)
235:     {
236:         case USART_STOP_BITS_1:
237:             /* Clear the STOP bit to set 1 stop bit*/
238:             addr->LCR &= LCR_STOP_BIT1;
239:             break;
240: 
241:         case USART_STOP_BITS_2:
242:             /*
243:             * If the STOP bit is set "1",we'd gotten 1.5 stop
244:             * bits when DLS(LCR[1:0]) is zero, else 2 stop bits.
245:             */
246:             addr->LCR |= LCR_STOP_BIT2;
247:             break;
248: 
249:         default:
250:             return ERR_USART(USART_ERROR_STOP_BITS);
251:     }
252: 
253:     return 0;
254: }

256: /**
257:   \brief       config usart data length.
258:   \param[in]   handle  usart handle to operate.
259:   \param[in]   databits      \ref usart_data_bits_e
260:   \return      error code
261: */
262: int32_t hal_usart_config_databits(usart_handle_t handle, usart_data_bits_e databits)
263: {
264:     USART_NULL_PARAM_CHK(handle);
265:     aic_usart_priv_t *usart_priv = handle;
266:     aic_usart_reg_t *addr = (aic_usart_reg_t *)(usart_priv->base);
267: 
268:     /* The word size decides by the DLS bits(LCR[1:0]), and the
269:      * corresponding relationship between them is:
270:      *   DLS   word size
271:      *       00 -- 5 bits
272:      *       01 -- 6 bits
273:      *       10 -- 7 bits
274:      *       11 -- 8 bits
275:      */
276: 
277:     switch (databits)
278:     {
279:         case USART_DATA_BITS_5:
280:             addr->LCR &= LCR_WORD_SIZE_5;
281:             break;
282: 
283:         case USART_DATA_BITS_6:
284:             addr->LCR &= 0xfd;
285:             addr->LCR |= LCR_WORD_SIZE_6;
286:             break;
287: 
288:         case USART_DATA_BITS_7:
289:             addr->LCR &= 0xfe;
290:             addr->LCR |= LCR_WORD_SIZE_7;
291:             break;
292: 
293:         case USART_DATA_BITS_8:
294:             addr->LCR |= LCR_WORD_SIZE_8;
295:             break;
296: 
297:         default:
298:             return ERR_USART(USART_ERROR_DATA_BITS);
299:     }
300: 
301:     return 0;
302: }

443: */
444: void hal_usart_intr_threshold_empty(int32_t idx, aic_usart_priv_t *usart_priv)
445: {
446:     if (usart_priv->tx_total_num == 0)
447:     {
448:         return;
449:     }

451:     volatile int i = 500;
