453: 
454:     if (usart_priv->tx_cnt >= usart_priv->tx_total_num) {
455:         addr->IER &= (~IER_THRE_INT_ENABLE);
456:         usart_priv->last_tx_num = usart_priv->tx_total_num;
457: 
458:         /* fix hardware bug */
459:         while (addr->USR & USR_UART_BUSY) {};
460: 
461:         i = 500;
462: 
463:         while (i--) {};
464: 
465:         usart_priv->tx_cnt = 0;
466:         usart_priv->tx_busy = 0;
467:         usart_priv->tx_buf = NULL;
468:         usart_priv->tx_total_num = 0;
469: 
470:         if (usart_priv->cb_event)
471:         {
472:             usart_priv->cb_event(idx, USART_EVENT_SEND_COMPLETE);
473:         }
474:     } else {
475:         /* fix hardware bug */
476:         while (addr->USR & USR_UART_BUSY) {};
477: 
478:         i = 500;
479: 
480:         while (i--) {};
481: 
482:         addr->THR = *((uint8_t *)usart_priv->tx_buf);
483:         usart_priv->tx_cnt++;
484:         usart_priv->tx_buf++;
485:     }

517: /**
518:   \brief        interrupt service function for receiver line.
519:   \param[in]   usart_priv usart private to operate.
520: */
521: static void hal_usart_intr_recv_line(int32_t idx, aic_usart_priv_t *usart_priv)
522: {
523:     aic_usart_reg_t *addr = (aic_usart_reg_t *)(usart_priv->base);
524:     uint32_t lsr_stat = addr->LSR;
525: 
526:     addr->IER &= (~IER_THRE_INT_ENABLE);
527: 
528:     uint32_t timecount = 0;
529: 
530:     while (addr->LSR & 0x1)
531:     {
532:         //addr->RBR;
533:         timecount++;
534: 
535:         if (timecount >= UART_BUSY_TIMEOUT)
536:         {
537:             if (usart_priv->cb_event)
538:             {
539:                 usart_priv->cb_event(idx, USART_EVENT_RX_TIMEOUT);
540:             }
541: 
542:             return;
543:         }
544:     }
545: 
546:     /** Break Interrupt bit. This is used to indicate the detection of a
547:       * break sequence on the serial input data.
548:       */
549:     if (lsr_stat & AIC_LSR_BI)
550:     {
551:         if (usart_priv->cb_event)
552:         {
553:             usart_priv->cb_event(idx, USART_EVENT_RX_BREAK);
554:         }
555: 
556:         return;
557:     }
558: 
559:     /** Framing Error bit. This is used to indicate the occurrence of a
560:       * framing error in the receiver. A framing error occurs when the receiver
561:       * does not detect a valid STOP bit in the received data.
562:       */
563:     if (lsr_stat & AIC_LSR_FE)
564:     {
565:         if (usart_priv->cb_event)
566:         {
567:             usart_priv->cb_event(idx, USART_EVENT_RX_FRAMING_ERROR);
568:         }
569: 
570:         return;
571:     }
572: 
573:     /** Framing Error bit. This is used to indicate the occurrence of a
574:       * framing error in the receiver. A framing error occurs when the
575:       * receiver does not detect a valid STOP bit in the received data.
576:       */
577:     if (lsr_stat & AIC_LSR_PE)
578:     {
579:         if (usart_priv->cb_event)
580:         {
581:             usart_priv->cb_event(idx, USART_EVENT_RX_PARITY_ERROR);
582:         }
583: 
584:         return;
585:     }
586: 
587:     /** Overrun error bit. This is used to indicate the occurrence of an overrun error.
588:       * This occurs if a new data character was received before the previous data was read.
589:       */
590:     if (lsr_stat & AIC_LSR_OE)
591:     {
592:         if (usart_priv->cb_event)
593:         {
594:             usart_priv->cb_event(idx, USART_EVENT_RX_OVERFLOW);
595:         }
596: 
597:         return;
598:     }
599: }

637: /**
638:   \brief       the interrupt service function.
639:   \param[in]   index of usart instance.
640: */
641: void hal_usart_irqhandler(int32_t idx)
642: {
643:     aic_usart_priv_t *usart_priv = &usart_instance[idx];
644:     aic_usart_reg_t *addr = (aic_usart_reg_t *)(usart_priv->base);
645: 
646:     uint8_t intr_state = addr->IIR & 0xf;
647: 
648:     switch (intr_state)
649:     {
650:         case AIC_IIR_THR_EMPTY:       /* interrupt source:transmitter holding register empty */
651:             hal_usart_intr_threshold_empty(idx, usart_priv);
652:             break;
653: 
654:         case AIC_IIR_RECV_DATA:       /* interrupt source:receiver data available or receiver fifo trigger level reached */
655:             hal_usart_intr_char_timeout(idx, usart_priv);
656:             //hal_usart_intr_recv_data(idx, usart_priv);
657:             break;
658: 
659:         case AIC_IIR_RECV_LINE:
660:             hal_usart_intr_recv_line(idx, usart_priv);
661:             break;
662: 
663:         case AIC_IIR_CHAR_TIMEOUT:
664:             hal_usart_intr_char_timeout(idx, usart_priv);
665:             break;
666: 
667:         default:
668:             break;
669:     }

743: /**
744:   \brief       config usart mode.
745:   \param[in]   handle  usart handle to operate.
746:   \param[in]   baud      baud rate
747:   \param[in]   mode      \ref usart_mode_e
748:   \param[in]   parity    \ref usart_parity_e
749:   \param[in]   stopbits  \ref usart_stop_bits_e
750:   \param[in]   bits      \ref usart_data_bits_e
751:   \return      error code
752: */
753: int32_t hal_usart_config(usart_handle_t handle,
754:                          uint32_t baud,
755:                          usart_mode_e mode,
756:                          usart_parity_e parity,
757:                          usart_stop_bits_e stopbits,
758:                          usart_data_bits_e bits,
759:                          usart_func_e func)
760: {
761:     int32_t ret;
762: 
763:     /* control the data_bit of the usart*/
764:     ret = hal_usart_config_baudrate(handle, baud);

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * D13x tinySPL Bootloader - system.c
3:  *
4:  * 完整的系统初始化：时钟、UART、SPI Flash、PSRAM
5:  * 地址来源: luban-lite aic_soc.h + D13x User Manual
6:  *
7:  ****************************************************************************/
8: 
9: #include <stdint.h>
10: #include "d13x_boot.h"
11: 
12: /****************************************************************************
13:  * CSR 寄存器访问 (来源: luban-lite core_rv32.h)
14:  ****************************************************************************/
15: 
16: /* T-Head E907 扩展 CSR */
17: 
18: #define CSR_MXSTATUS     0x7C0
19: #define CSR_MEXSTATUS    0x7C1
20: #define CSR_MSTATUS      0x300
21: #define CSR_MTVEC        0x305
22: #define CSR_MTVT         0x7C0
23: 
24: /****************************************************************************
25:  * SystemInit (来源: luban-lite system.c)
26:  * 由 startup.S 在 BSS 清零后调用
27:  ****************************************************************************/
28: 
29: void SystemInit(void)
30: {
31:   /* 使能 mstatus FS (FPU) */
32: 
33:   uint32_t mstatus;
34:   __asm__ __volatile__("csrr %0, mstatus" : "=r"(mstatus));
35:   mstatus |= (1 << 13);  /* FS = 01 (Initial) */
36:   __asm__ __volatile__("csrw mstatus, %0" :: "r"(mstatus));
37: 
38:   /* 使能 mxstatus THEADISAEE (T-Head ISA 扩展) */
39: 
40:   uint32_t mxstatus;
41:   __asm__ __volatile__("csrr %0, 0x7C0" : "=r"(mxstatus));
42:   mxstatus |= (1 << 22);  /* THEADISAEE */
43:   mxstatus |= (1 << 15);  /* MM (Memory Management) */
44:   __asm__ __volatile__("csrw 0x7C0, %0" :: "r"(mxstatus));
45: 
46:   /* 使能 mexstatus SPUSHEN/SPSWAPEN */
47: 
48:   uint32_t mexstatus;
49:   __asm__ __volatile__("csrr %0, 0x7C1" : "=r"(mexstatus));
50:   mexstatus |= (1 << 16);  /* SPUSHEN */
51:   mexstatus |= (1 << 17);  /* SPSWAPEN */
52:   __asm__ __volatile__("csrw 0x7C1, %0" :: "r"(mexstatus));
53: }
54: 
55: /****************************************************************************
56:  * 寄存器访问宏
57:  ****************************************************************************/
58: 
59: #define getreg32(a)     (*(volatile uint32_t *)(a))
60: #define putreg32(v,a)   (*(volatile uint32_t *)(a) = (v))
61: 
62: /****************************************************************************
63:  * 外设基地址 (来源: luban-lite aic_soc.h)
64:  ****************************************************************************/
65: 
66: #define CMU_BASE        0x18020000
67: #define GPIO_BASE       0x18700000
68: #define UART0_BASE      0x18710000
69: #define XSPI_BASE       0x10300000  /* XSPI PSRAM 控制器 */
70: #define QSPI0_BASE      0x10400000  /* QSPI0 SPI Flash */
71: #define WDT_BASE        0x19000000  /* Watchdog */
72: #define SID_BASE        0x19010000  /* eFuse */
73: 
74: /****************************************************************************
75:  * PSRAM 配置 (D13x)
76:  ****************************************************************************/
77: 
78: #define PSRAM_BASE          0x40000000
79: #define PSRAM_SIZE          (8 * 1024 * 1024)  /* 8MB */
80: 
81: /* eFuse 寄存器 */
82: 
83: #define EFUSE_CMU_REG       (CMU_BASE + 0x904)
84: #define EFUSE_218_REG       (SID_BASE + 0x218)
85: #define EFUSE_224_REG       (SID_BASE + 0x224)
86: 
87: /* PSRAM 芯片 ID */
88: 
89: #define PSRAM_CHIP_APS3208K 0x80c9
90: #define PSRAM_CHIP_SCKW18   0xc59a
91: #define PSRAM_CHIP_APS12816 0xdd8d
92: 
93: /****************************************************************************
94:  * 时钟系统 (CMU)
95:  ****************************************************************************/
96: 
97: void d13x_clock_init(void)
98: {
99:   uint32_t reg;
100: 
101:   /* 打开 24MHz 振荡器 */
102: 
103:   reg = getreg32(CMU_BASE + 0x0A4);
104:   reg |= (1 << 1);
105:   putreg32(reg, CMU_BASE + 0x0A4);
106: 
107:   /* PLL 公共电路 LDO */
108: 
109:   reg = getreg32(CMU_BASE + 0x0A0);
110:   reg |= (1 << 31) | (1 << 0);
111:   putreg32(reg, CMU_BASE + 0x0A0);
112: 
113:   /* PLL_INT1 → 1.2GHz */
114: 
115:   putreg32(0x240C4040, CMU_BASE + 0x044);
116:   while (!(getreg32(CMU_BASE + 0x044) & (1 << 17)));
117: 
118:   /* PLL_INT0 → 480MHz */
119: 
120:   putreg32(0x240C4040, CMU_BASE + 0x040);
121:   while (!(getreg32(CMU_BASE + 0x040) & (1 << 17)));
122: 
123:   /* 总线时钟 */
124: 
125:   putreg32(0x00000001, CMU_BASE + 0x100);
126:   putreg32(0x00000001, CMU_BASE + 0x120);
127:   putreg32(0x00000100, CMU_BASE + 0x200);
128: 
129:   /* GPIO/UART 时钟 */
130: 
131:   reg = getreg32(CMU_BASE + 0x83C);
132:   reg |= (1 << 12) | (1 << 13);
133:   putreg32(reg, CMU_BASE + 0x83C);
134:   putreg32(0x00001001, CMU_BASE + 0x840);
135: 
136:   /* QSPI0 时钟: 释放复位 + 使能总线时钟 + 使能模块时钟 */
137: 
138:   putreg32((1 << 13) | (1 << 12) | (1 << 8), CMU_BASE + 0x460);

210: static void d13x_spi_init(void)
211: {
212:   /* 复位控制器 */
213: 
214:   putreg32(QSPI_CFG_RST, QSPI_CFG);
215:   while (getreg32(QSPI_CFG) & QSPI_CFG_RST);

217:   /* 使能控制器 + 主机模式 */

219:   putreg32(QSPI_CFG_EN | QSPI_CFG_MASTER, QSPI_CFG);

223: 
224:   putreg32(15, QSPI_CCFG);

227: 
228:   putreg32(QSPI_TCFG_CS_SW | QSPI_TCFG_CS_HIGH, QSPI_TCFG);

236: {
237:   uint32_t reg = getreg32(QSPI_TCFG);
238:   if (assert)

241:     reg |= QSPI_TCFG_CS_HIGH;

245: static void d13x_spi_txrx(uint8_t *tx, uint8_t *rx, int len)

249:     {
250:       /* 写入 TX FIFO */
251: 
252:       putreg32(tx ? tx[i] : 0, QSPI_TXD);

254:       /* 启动传输 */

256:       uint32_t tcfg = getreg32(QSPI_TCFG);
257:       putreg32(tcfg | QSPI_TCFG_START, QSPI_TCFG);

261:       while (!(getreg32(QSPI_FSTS) & QSPI_FSTS_TD));

# D13x OpenVela NuttX Integration Correctness Report

I have completed a thorough review of all five integration files plus `chip.h`, cross-referencing against NuttX RISC-V headers, Kconfig, and every other RISC-V port in this tree.

---

## ISSUE 1 — CRITICAL: No NuttX Assembly Startup (missing head.S)

**Location**: `/home/lladlam/OpenVela/openvela/vendor/artinchip/chips/d13x/artinchip_start.c`, line 461

The D13x defines `__start` as a C function. Every single other RISC-V port in NuttX (bl602, c906, sg2000, qemu-rv, k210, hpm6750, fe310, mpfs, esp32c3, litex, jh7110, etc.) defines `__start` as an **assembly label** in a `head.S` file that:

1. Disables interrupts (`csrc mstatus, MSTATUS_MIE`)
2. Loads `gp` (global pointer)
3. Loads `sp` (stack pointer) to top of IDLE stack
4. Zeros the BSS section in assembly
5. Copies .data from flash to RAM in assembly
6. Then calls a C init function that ultimately invokes `nx_start()`

The vendor directory contains no `.S` file for D13x. The luban-lite `startup_gcc.S` at `/home/lladlam/OpenVela/luban-lite/bsp/artinchip/sys/d13x/startup_gcc.S` targets RT-Thread (calls `SystemInit` then `main`), not NuttX.

**Consequence**: Without assembly setting up `sp` before any C code runs, the linker entry point has no valid stack, and the C function `__start` cannot execute. BSS/data init done inside the C function is also conceptually wrong because C runtime requires BSS to be cleared *before* entering C code.

**Fix**: Create a `d13x_head.S` modeled after other RISC-V ports. It should set up `gp`, `sp`, clear BSS, copy .data, then call a C init function. Move the hardware initialization (clock, UART, PSRAM, watchdog) into that C function, which then calls `nx_start()`.

---

## ISSUE 2 — MEDIUM: `riscv_dispatch_irq` Signature Uses `uint32_t` Instead of `uintreg_t`

**Location**: `artinchip_irq.c`, line 187

```
D13x:      void *riscv_dispatch_irq(uint32_t mcause, uint32_t *regs)
c906:      void *riscv_dispatch_irq(uintptr_t vector, uintptr_t *regs)
bl602:     void *riscv_dispatch_irq(uintreg_t vector, uintreg_t *regs)
D12x:      void *riscv_dispatch_irq(uintptr_t vector, uintptr_t *regs)
sg2000:    void *riscv_dispatch_irq(uintptr_t vector, uintptr_t *regs)
```

All other ports use `uintreg_t` or `uintptr_t`. Per `/home/lladlam/OpenVela/openvela/nuttx/arch/risc-v/include/types.h` line 80, `uintreg_t` is `uint32_t` on RV32, so this is *binary-compatible* on the D13x E907 (32-bit) core. However, it diverges from the NuttX coding convention and would break if the code were ever ported to an RV64 core.

Additionally, the D13x calls `irq_dispatch(irq, regs)` directly (line 197), whereas most other ports call `riscv_doirq(irq, regs)` which handles context switching. The D13x version returns `regs` directly without going through `riscv_doirq`. This is a functional concern -- `irq_dispatch` dispatches the handler but does not perform the context-switch plumbing that `riscv_doirq` does.

---

## ISSUE 3 — MEDIUM: `up_irq_enable` Implements Non-CLIC Logic But CLIC Is Used

**Location**: `artinchip_irq.c`, lines 210-222

The D13x CLIC interrupt controller is used throughout the file (mtvec mode 3, mtvt, CLICINT registers), and `irq.h` defines `up_irq_save`/`up_irq_restore` to manipulate `CSR_INTTHRESH` when `CONFIG_ARCH_RV_HAVE_CLIC` is set (lines 840-861 of irq.h).

Yet the D13x `up_irq_enable()` manipulates `mstatus` via inline assembly (bit 3 = MIE), which is the non-CLIC path. When `CONFIG_ARCH_RV_HAVE_CLIC` is enabled, interrupt gating should be done through the CLIC threshold CSR (`CSR_INTTHRESH`), not `mstatus.MIE`. The NuttX `irq.h` provides CLIC-aware `up_irq_save`/`up_irq_restore` for exactly this purpose.

If `CONFIG_ARCH_RV_HAVE_CLIC` is not set in the D13x config, the `mstatus` approach works but then the mtvec/mtvt setup in `up_irqinitialize` (using CLIC mode 3) becomes inconsistent -- you cannot use CLIC vectoring without also using CLIC for interrupt masking.

---

## ISSUE 4 — LOW: `up_allocate_heap` Missing `FAR` Qualifier

**Location**: `artinchip_allocateheap.c`, line 38

```
Header:  void up_allocate_heap(FAR void **heap_start, size_t *heap_size)
D13x:    void up_allocate_heap(void **heap_start, size_t *heap_size)
```

The `FAR` macro is `#define FAR` (empty) in flat build, so this compiles identically. However, in kernel/user-space builds (`CONFIG_BUILD_KERNEL` or `CONFIG_BUILD_PROTECTED`), `FAR` resolves to an address-space qualifier. Omitting it is a coding standard violation though functionally benign in the expected flat-build configuration.

---

## ISSUE 5 — LOW: Oneshot `start()` Writes to Counter Register as Comparison Value

**Location**: `artinchip_oneshot.c`, lines 110-117

```c
static void d13x_oneshot_start(struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *lower, clkcnt_t delay)
{
  uint32_t now_lo = getreg32(GTC_CNTVL);
  uint32_t cmp = now_lo + (uint32_t)delay;
  putreg32(cmp, GTC_CNTVL);  /* writes to the counter value register */
}
```

The code writes the comparison target back into `GTC_CNTVL`, which is the *counter value* register (offset 0x0008), not a compare register. There is no separate compare register defined in the GTC register map (lines 26-33). Writing to `GTC_CNTVL` would overwrite the running counter, not set a comparison threshold. This means the timer interrupt may never fire unless the hardware implicitly uses `GTC_CNTVL` as both counter-read and compare-write (some timer controllers do this, but the comments suggest otherwise).

Similarly, `d13x_oneshot_cancel` writes `0xFFFFFFFF` to `GTC_CNTVL` (line 144), which would corrupt the running counter.

22: /* CLIC 寄存器结构 (来源: luban-lite core_rv32.h CLIC_Type)
23:  *
24:  * CLIC 基地址: 0x20800000
25:  * 每个中断源占 4 字节: IP(1B), IE(1B), ATTR(1B), CTL(1B)
26:  * CLICINT[] 数组起始偏移: 0x1000
27:  *
28:  * struct CLIC_Type {
29:  *   uint32_t CLICCFG;      // offset 0x000
30:  *   uint32_t CLICINFO;     // offset 0x004
31:  *   uint32_t MINTTHRESH;   // offset 0x008
32:  *   uint32_t RESERVED[1021];
33:  *   CLIC_INT_Control CLICINT[4096];  // offset 0x1000
34:  * };
35:  *
36:  * struct CLIC_INT_Control {
37:  *   uint8_t IP;    // offset +0x000 (pending)
38:  *   uint8_t IE;    // offset +0x004 (enable)
39:  *   uint8_t ATTR;  // offset +0x008 (attribute: vector/shv)
40:  *   uint8_t CTL;   // offset +0x00C (control: priority)
41:  * };
42:  */
43: 
44: #define D13X_CLIC_BASE         D13X_E907_CLIC_BASE   /* 0x20800000 */
45: #define D13X_CLIC_CFG          (D13X_CLIC_BASE + 0x0000)
46: #define D13X_CLIC_INFO         (D13X_CLIC_BASE + 0x0004)
47: #define D13X_CLIC_MINTTHRESH   (D13X_CLIC_BASE + 0x0008)
48: #define D13X_CLIC_INT_BASE     (D13X_CLIC_BASE + 0x1000)  /* CLICINT[] 起始 */
49:

101: 
102: /****************************************************************************
103:  * Name: up_irqinitialize
104:  *
105:  * Description:
106:  *   Initialize the interrupt subsystem
107:  *
108:  ****************************************************************************/
109: 
110: void up_irqinitialize(void)
111: {
112:   int i;
113: 
114:   /* 配置 mtvec (mode 3) + mtvt 双 CSR */
115: 
116:   uint32_t mtvec = (uint32_t)__trap_vec | 0x3;
117:   __asm__ __volatile__("csrw mtvec, %0" :: "r"(mtvec));
118: 
119:   /* mtvt CSR (T-Head 扩展，CSR 编号 0x7C0) */
120: 
121:   uint32_t mtvt = (uint32_t)__trap_vec;
122:   __asm__ __volatile__("csrw 0x7C0, %0" :: "r"(mtvt));
123: 
124:   /* 初始化 CLIC 中断控制器 (来源: luban-lite system.c SystemInit) */
125: 
126:   /* 读取 CLIC 配置信息 */
127: 
128:   volatile uint32_t *cliccfg = (volatile uint32_t *)D13X_CLIC_CFG;
129:   volatile uint32_t *clicinfo = (volatile uint32_t *)D13X_CLIC_INFO;
130: 
131:   uint32_t info = *clicinfo;
132:   uint32_t nlbits = (info >> 21) & 0xF;
133: 
134:   *cliccfg = (nlbits << 1) & 0x1E;
135: 
136:   /* 初始化所有中断: 清除 pending, 使能向量中断 */
137: 
138:   for (i = 0; i < MAX_IRQn; i++)
139:     {
140:       d13x_clic_clear_pending(i);
141:       d13x_clic_set_attr(i, 1);  /* use vector interrupt */
142:     }
143: 
144:   /* tspend 使用正向中断 (来源: luban-lite system.c) */
145: 
146:   d13x_clic_set_attr(Machine_Software_IRQn, 0x3);
147: 
148:   /* 使能全局中断 */
149: 
150:   up_irq_enable();
151: }
152: 
153: /****************************************************************************
154:  * Name: up_enable_irq
155:  *
156:  * Description:
157:  *   Enable the interrupt specified by 'irq'
158:  *
159:  ****************************************************************************/
160: 
161: void up_enable_irq(int irq)
162: {
163:   d13x_clic_enable_irq(irq);
164: }
165: 
166: /****************************************************************************
167:  * Name: up_disable_irq
168:  *
169:  * Description:
170:  *   Disable the interrupt specified by 'irq'
171:  *
172:  ****************************************************************************/
173: 
174: void up_disable_irq(int irq)
175: {
176:   d13x_clic_disable_irq(irq);
177: }
178: 
179: /****************************************************************************
180:  * Name: riscv_dispatch_irq
181:  *
182:  * Description:
183:  *   Process interrupt and dispatch to registered handler
184:  *
185:  ****************************************************************************/
186: 
187: void *riscv_dispatch_irq(uint32_t mcause, uint32_t *regs)
188: {
189:   int irq;
190: 
191:   /* 读取中断号 */
192: 
193:   irq = (int)(mcause & 0x7FFFFFFF);
194: 
195:   /* 调用中断处理函数 */
196: 
197:   irq_dispatch(irq, regs);
198: 
199:   return regs;
200: }
201: 
202: /****************************************************************************
203:  * Name: up_irq_enable
204:  *
205:  * Description:
206:  *   Enable all interrupts
207:  *
208:  ****************************************************************************/
209: 
210: irqstate_t up_irq_enable(void)
211: {
212:   irqstate_t flags;
213: 
214:   /* 读取当前中断状态 */
215: 
216:   __asm__ __volatile__("csrr %0, mstatus" : "=r"(flags));
217: 
218:   /* 使能中断 */
219: 
220:   __asm__ __volatile__("csrsi mstatus, 0x8");
221: 
222:   return flags;
223: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * vendor/artinchip/chips/d13x/artinchip_oneshot.c
3:  *
4:  * D13x 定时器驱动（arch_alarm 模型）
5:  * GTC 寄存器来源: D13x User Manual §11.1 + luban-lite
6:  *
7:  ****************************************************************************/
8: 
9: /****************************************************************************
10:  * Included Files
11:  ****************************************************************************/
12: 
13: #include <nuttx/config.h>
14: #include <nuttx/timers/oneshot.h>
15: #include <nuttx/timers/arch_alarm.h>
16: #include <nuttx/irq.h>
17: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
18: #include "chip.h"
19: 
20: /****************************************************************************
21:  * Pre-processor Definitions
22:  ****************************************************************************/
23: 
24: /* GTC 寄存器偏移 (来源: D13x User Manual §11.1.3 表 11-1) */
25: 
26: #define GTC_CNTCR                (D13X_GTC_BASE + 0x0000)  /* 计数器控制 */
27: #define GTC_CNTSR                (D13X_GTC_BASE + 0x0004)  /* 计数器状态 */
28: #define GTC_CNTVL                (D13X_GTC_BASE + 0x0008)  /* 计数值低位 [31:0] */
29: #define GTC_CNTVH                (D13X_GTC_BASE + 0x000C)  /* 计数值高位 [51:32] */
30: #define GTC_CNTFID0              (D13X_GTC_BASE + 0x0020)  /* 计数频率 ID0 = 4MHz */
31: #define GTC_CNTFID1              (D13X_GTC_BASE + 0x0024)  /* 计数频率 ID1 = 1MHz */
32: #define GTC_CNTFID2              (D13X_GTC_BASE + 0x0028)  /* 计数频率 ID2 = 250KHz */
33: #define GTC_CONFG                (D13X_GTC_BASE + 0x00C0)  /* 配置: FDIV 分频 */
34: 
35: /* GTC_CNTCR 位定义 */
36: 
37: #define GTC_CNTCR_EN             (1 << 0)   /* 计数器使能 */
38: #define GTC_CNTCR_HDBG           (1 << 1)   /* 调试时保持 */
39: 
40: /* GTC 中断号: GTC 通过 CLIC 直接产生中断，IRQ 号取决于硬件连线
41:  * luban-lite 使用 CORET (IRQ 7) 作为系统 tick，GTC 仅用于使能计数
42:  * NuttX arch_alarm 模型需要一个 IRQ，使用 CORET_IRQn (7) 或
43:  * 通过 oneshot 软件比较实现。此处使用 CORET_IRQn 作为中断源。
44:  */
45: 
46: #define D13X_IRQ_GTC             7   /* CORET_IRQn, 与 luban-lite 一致 */
47: 
48: /* GTC 时钟频率: 基频 4MHz (D13x User Manual §11.1.1)
49:  * PCLK 可选 12/24/48/60 MHz，GTC 内部分频到 4MHz 基频
50:  * luban-lite system.c 中: *(volatile uint32_t *)GTC_BASE = 0x0001 (使能)
51:  * 计数频率由 GTC_CONFG 的 FDIV 字段控制
52:  */
53: 
54: #define GTC_BASE_FREQ            4000000    /* 4MHz 基频 */
55: 
56: /****************************************************************************
57:  * Private Types
58:  ****************************************************************************/
59: 
60: struct d13x_oneshot_lowerhalf_s
61: {
62:   struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s lower;
63: };
64: 
65: /****************************************************************************
66:  * Private Data
67:  ****************************************************************************/
68: 
69: static struct d13x_oneshot_lowerhalf_s g_d13x_oneshot;
70: 
71: /****************************************************************************
72:  * Private Functions
73:  ****************************************************************************/
74: 
75: /****************************************************************************
76:  * Name: d13x_oneshot_current
77:  *
78:  * Description:
79:  *   Get the current timer value (clkcnt_t API)
80:  *
81:  ****************************************************************************/
82: 
83: static clkcnt_t d13x_oneshot_current(struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *lower)
84: {
85:   /* 读取 64-bit 计数值: 先读高 32 位，再读低 32 位，再读高 32 位
86:    * 如果高 32 位变化了，说明发生了进位，需要重读
87:    */
88: 
89:   uint32_t high1, low, high2;
90: 
91:   do
92:     {
93:       high1 = getreg32(GTC_CNTVH);
94:       low   = getreg32(GTC_CNTVL);
95:       high2 = getreg32(GTC_CNTVH);
96:     }
97:   while (high1 != high2);
98: 
99:   return (clkcnt_t)(((uint64_t)high1 << 32) | low);
100: }
101: 
102: /****************************************************************************
103:  * Name: d13x_oneshot_start
104:  *
105:  * Description:
106:  *   Start the oneshot timer with a relative delay (clkcnt_t API)
107:  *
108:  ****************************************************************************/
109: 
110: static void d13x_oneshot_start(struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *lower,
111:                                clkcnt_t delay)
112: {
113:   uint32_t now_lo = getreg32(GTC_CNTVL);
114:   uint32_t cmp = now_lo + (uint32_t)delay;
115: 
116:   putreg32(cmp, GTC_CNTVL);  /* 写入比较值到低 32 位 */
117: }
118: 
119: /****************************************************************************
120:  * Name: d13x_oneshot_start_absolute
121:  *
122:  * Description:
123:  *   Start the oneshot timer with an absolute counter value (clkcnt_t API)
124:  *
125:  ****************************************************************************/
126: 
127: static void d13x_oneshot_start_absolute(struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *lower,
128:                                         clkcnt_t cnt)
129: {
130:   putreg32((uint32_t)cnt, GTC_CNTVL);
131: }
132: 
133: /****************************************************************************
134:  * Name: d13x_oneshot_cancel
135:  *
136:  * Description:
137:  *   Cancel the oneshot timer (clkcnt_t API)
138:  *
139:  ****************************************************************************/
140: 
141: static void d13x_oneshot_cancel(struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *lower)
142: {
143:   /* 清除比较匹配: 写入一个不会匹配的值 */
144:   putreg32(0xFFFFFFFF, GTC_CNTVL);
145: }
146: 
147: /****************************************************************************
148:  * Name: d13x_oneshot_maxdelay
149:  *
150:  * Description:
151:  *   Get the maximum delay value (clkcnt_t API)
152:  *
153:  ****************************************************************************/
154: 
155: static clkcnt_t d13x_oneshot_maxdelay(struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *lower)
156: {
157:   return (clkcnt_t)0xFFFFFFFF;
158: }
159: 
160: /****************************************************************************
161:  * Name: d13x_oneshot_handler
162:  *
163:  * Description:
164:  *   Timer interrupt handler (CORET_IRQn)
165:  *
166:  ****************************************************************************/
167: 
168: static int d13x_oneshot_handler(int irq, FAR void *context, FAR void *arg)
169: {
170:   struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *lower = arg;
171: 
172:   /* 调用上层回调 */
173: 
174:   if (lower->callback)
175:     {
176:       lower->callback(lower, lower->arg);
177:     }
178: 
179:   return OK;
180: }
181: 
182: /****************************************************************************
183:  * Private Data
184:  ****************************************************************************/
185: 
186: static const struct oneshot_operations_s g_d13x_oneshot_ops =
187: {
188:   .current        = d13x_oneshot_current,
189:   .start          = d13x_oneshot_start,
190:   .start_absolute = d13x_oneshot_start_absolute,
191:   .cancel         = d13x_oneshot_cancel,
192:   .max_delay      = d13x_oneshot_maxdelay,
193: };
194: 
195: /****************************************************************************
196:  * Public Functions
197:  ****************************************************************************/
198: 
199: /****************************************************************************
200:  * Name: up_timer_initialize
201:  *
202:  * Description:
203:  *   This function is called during start-up to initialize the timer
204:  *   interrupt.
205:  *
206:  ****************************************************************************/
207: 
208: void up_timer_initialize(void)
209: {
210:   /* 使能 GTC 计数器 (来源: luban-lite system.c aic_gtc_enable) */
211: 
212:   putreg32(GTC_CNTCR_EN, GTC_CNTCR);
213: 
214:   /* 绑定中断处理函数 (使用 CORET_IRQn, 与 luban-lite 一致) */
215: 
216:   irq_attach(D13X_IRQ_GTC, d13x_oneshot_handler, &g_d13x_oneshot.lower);
217:   up_enable_irq(D13X_IRQ_GTC);
218: 
219:   /* 初始化 oneshot 计数器，使用 4MHz 基频 */
220: 
221:   oneshot_count_init(&g_d13x_oneshot.lower, GTC_BASE_FREQ);
222: 
223:   /* 创建 oneshot 实例并绑定系统定时器 */
224: 
225:   g_d13x_oneshot.lower.ops = &g_d13x_oneshot_ops;
226:   up_alarm_set_lowerhalf(&g_d13x_oneshot.lower);
227: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * vendor/artinchip/chips/d13x/artinchip_start.c
3:  *
4:  * D13x 启动入口
5:  * 地址来源: luban-lite aic_soc.h + D13x User Manual
6:  *
7:  ****************************************************************************/
8: 
9: /****************************************************************************
10:  * Included Files
11:  ****************************************************************************/
12: 
13: #include <nuttx/config.h>
14: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
15: #include <nuttx/irq.h>
16: #include <nuttx/init.h>
17: #include <arch/board/board.h>
18: #include "chip.h"
19: 
20: /****************************************************************************
21:  * Pre-processor Definitions
22:  ****************************************************************************/
23: 
24: /* CMU 寄存器地址 (来源: luban-lite aic_soc.h CMU_BASE=0x18020000) */
25: 
26: #define CMU_PLL_IN          (D13X_CMU_BASE + 0x0A4)
27: #define CMU_PLL_COM         (D13X_CMU_BASE + 0x0A0)
28: #define CMU_PLL_INT0_GEN    (D13X_CMU_BASE + 0x000)
29: #define CMU_PLL_INT0_CFG    (D13X_CMU_BASE + 0x040)
30: #define CMU_PLL_INT1_GEN    (D13X_CMU_BASE + 0x004)
31: #define CMU_PLL_INT1_CFG    (D13X_CMU_BASE + 0x044)
32: #define CMU_CLK_CPU         (D13X_CMU_BASE + 0x200)
33: #define CMU_CLK_AXI_AHB     (D13X_CMU_BASE + 0x100)
34: #define CMU_CLK_APB0        (D13X_CMU_BASE + 0x120)
35: #define CMU_CLK_UART0       (D13X_CMU_BASE + 0x840)
36: #define CMU_CLK_GPIO        (D13X_CMU_BASE + 0x83C)
37: 
38: /* eFuse 寄存器 (来源: luban-lite aic_soc.h SID_BASE=0x19010000) */
39: 
40: #define EFUSE_CMU_REG       (D13X_CMU_BASE + 0x904)
41: #define EFUSE_218_REG       (D13X_SID_BASE + 0x218)
42: 
43: /* WDOG 寄存器 (来源: D13x User Manual §11.2, luban-lite aic_soc.h WDT_BASE=0x19000000)
44:  *
45:  * WDOG_CTL  = base + 0x000  (Control: enable, debug continue, write protection)
46:  * WDOG_CNT  = base + 0x004  (Counter value, 32K clock cycles)
47:  * IRQ_EN    = base + 0x008  (Interrupt enable)
48:  * IRQ_STA   = base + 0x00C  (Interrupt status, W1C)
49:  * WDOG_OP   = base + 0x0E8  (Operation command)
50:  */
51: 
52: #define WDOG_CTL            (D13X_WDT_BASE + 0x000)
53: #define WDOG_CNT            (D13X_WDT_BASE + 0x004)
54: #define WDOG_IRQ_EN         (D13X_WDT_BASE + 0x008)
55: #define WDOG_IRQ_STA        (D13X_WDT_BASE + 0x00C)
56: #define WDOG_OP             (D13X_WDT_BASE + 0x0E8)
57: 
58: /* WDOG_CTL 位定义 */
59: 
60: #define WDOG_CTL_EN         (1 << 0)   /* 看门狗使能 */
61: #define WDOG_CTL_DBG_HALT   (1 << 1)   /* 调试时暂停 */
62: #define WDOG_CTL_W_PROT     (1 << 4)   /* 写保护 */
63: 
64: /* BSS 段符号 */
65: 
66: extern uint32_t _sbss[];
67: extern uint32_t _ebss[];
68: extern uint32_t _sdata[];
69: extern uint32_t _edata[];
70: extern uint32_t _eronly[];
71: 
72: /* 启动参数位域定义 */
73: 
74: #define get_boot_device(var)      ((var) & 0xF)
75: #define get_boot_controller(var)  (((var) >> 4) & 0xF)
76: #define get_boot_reason(var)      (((var) >> 8) & 0xF)
77: #define get_boot_image_id(var)    (((var) >> 12) & 0xF)
78: 
79: /****************************************************************************
80:  * Private Functions
81:  ****************************************************************************/
82: 
83: static void d13x_clock_init(void)
84: {
85:   uint32_t reg;
86: 
87:   /* 1. 打开 24MHz 振荡器 */
88: 
89:   reg = getreg32(CMU_PLL_IN);
90:   reg |= (1 << 1);
91:   putreg32(reg, CMU_PLL_IN);
92: 
93:   /* 2. PLL 公共电路 LDO */
94: 
95:   reg = getreg32(CMU_PLL_COM);
96:   reg |= (1 << 31);
97:   reg |= (1 << 0);
98:   putreg32(reg, CMU_PLL_COM);
99: 
100:   /* 3. 配置 PLL_INT1 → 1.2GHz (N=49) */
101: 
102:   putreg32(0x240C4040, CMU_PLL_INT1_CFG);
103: 
104:   /* 等待 PLL 锁定 */
105: 
106:   while (!(getreg32(CMU_PLL_INT1_CFG) & (1 << 17)));
107: 
108:   /* 4. 配置 PLL_INT0 → 480MHz (N=19) */
109: 
110:   putreg32(0x240C4040, CMU_PLL_INT0_CFG);
111: 
112:   /* 等待 PLL 锁定 */
113: 
114:   while (!(getreg32(CMU_PLL_INT0_CFG) & (1 << 17)));
115: 
116:   /* 5. 总线时钟: AXI/AHB = 200MHz, APB0 = 100MHz */
117: 
118:   putreg32(0x00000001, CMU_CLK_AXI_AHB);
119:   putreg32(0x00000001, CMU_CLK_APB0);
120: 
121:   /* 6. CPU 时钟: 480MHz */
122: 
123:   putreg32(0x00000100, CMU_CLK_CPU);
124: 
125:   /* 7. 打开 GPIO 时钟 */
126: 
127:   reg = getreg32(CMU_CLK_GPIO);
128:   reg |= (1 << 12);
129:   reg |= (1 << 13);
130:   putreg32(reg, CMU_CLK_GPIO);
131: 
132:   /* 8. 打开 UART0 时钟: 60MHz */
133: 
134:   putreg32(0x00001001, CMU_CLK_UART0);
135: }
136: 
137: static void d13x_uart_init(void)
138: {
139:   uint32_t divisor;
140: 
141:   /* 配置 UART0 引脚复用: PA0→TX, PA1→RX (PIN_FUN=5) */
142:   /* TODO: 配置 GPIO 引脚复用寄存器 (需要查看 luban-lite pinmux) */
143: 
144:   /* 配置波特率 115200: divisor = 60MHz / (16 × 115200) ≈ 32 */
145: 
146:   divisor = D13X_UART0_FREQ / (16 * D13X_UART0_BAUDRATE);
147: 
148:   /* 禁用 UART */
149: 
150:   putreg32(0, D13X_UART0_BASE + UART_LCR);
151: 
152:   /* 配置波特率 */
153: 
154:   putreg32(divisor & 0xFF, D13X_UART0_BASE + UART_RBR_THR_DLL);
155:   putreg32((divisor >> 8) & 0xFF, D13X_UART0_BASE + UART_DLH);
156: 
157:   /* 使能 FIFO */
158: 
159:   putreg32(UART_FCR_FIFOE | UART_FCR_RFIFOR | UART_FCR_XFIFOR,
160:            D13X_UART0_BASE + UART_FCR);
161: 
162:   /* 配置 8N1: 8 数据位, 1 停止位, 无校验 */
163: 
164:   putreg32(0x03, D13X_UART0_BASE + UART_LCR);
165: }
166: 
167: /****************************************************************************
168:  * PSRAM 驱动 (D13x)
169:  * XSPI 基地址: 0x10300000 (来源: luban-lite aic_soc.h)
170:  ****************************************************************************/
171: 
172: /* XSPI 控制器寄存器 */
173: 
174: #define XSPI_CFG            (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x000)
175: #define XSPI_TIMING         (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x004)
176: #define XSPI_CFG2           (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x008)
177: #define XSPI_CMD            (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x100)
178: #define XSPI_ADDR           (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x104)
179: #define XSPI_DATA           (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x108)
180: #define XSPI_CFG3           (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x10C)
181: #define XSPI_STATUS         (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x110)
182: #define XSPI_CTRL           (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x114)
183: #define XSPI_BCNT           (D13X_XSPI_BASE + 0x118)
184: 
185: /* XSPI 配置位 */
186: 
187: #define XSPI_CFG_EN         (1 << 0)
188: #define XSPI_CFG_RST        (1 << 1)
189: #define XSPI_CFG_CLK_EN     (1 << 2)
190: 
191: /* XSPI 状态位 */
192: 
193: #define XSPI_STATUS_BUSY    (1 << 0)
194: #define XSPI_STATUS_DONE    (1 << 1)
195: 
196: /* PSRAM 命令 */
197: 
198: #define PSRAM_CMD_RESET     0xFF
199: #define PSRAM_CMD_READ_ID   0x40
200: #define PSRAM_CMD_WRITE_MR  0xC0
201: #define PSRAM_CMD_READ_MR   0x40
202: 
203: /* PSRAM 模式寄存器 */
204: 
205: #define PSRAM_MR0           0x00
206: #define PSRAM_MR4           0x04
207: 
208: static uint32_t d13x_psram_read_efuse(uint32_t reg_addr)
209: {
210:   /* 使能 eFuse 时钟 */
211: 
212:   putreg32(0x1100, EFUSE_CMU_REG);
213: 
214:   /* 读取 eFuse 值 */
215: 
216:   uint32_t val = getreg32(reg_addr);
217: 
218:   /* 关闭 eFuse 时钟 */
219: 
220:   putreg32(0x0, EFUSE_CMU_REG);
221: 
222:   return val;
223: }
224: 
225: static uint32_t d13x_psram_get_size(void)
226: {
227:   uint32_t fuse_218 = d13x_psram_read_efuse(EFUSE_218_REG);
228:   uint8_t mark_id = fuse_218 & 0xFF;
229: 
230:   /* 根据 mark_id 确定 PSRAM 大小 */
231: 
232:   switch (mark_id)
233:     {
234:       case 0x00:  /* force use cfg0 */
235:         return 0;
236:       case 0x01:  /* D131BAS 4M */
237:         return 4 * 1024 * 1024;
238:       case 0x02:  /* D131BBS 8M */
239:       case 0x03:  /* D131CBS 8M */
240:       case 0x04:  /* D131EBS/D133EBS 8M */

733: /* Return program counter */
734: 
735: static inline_function uintptr_t up_getpc(void)
736: {
737:   register uintptr_t pc;
738:   __asm__
739:   (
740:     "\tauipc %0, 0\n"
741:     : "=r"(pc)
742:   );
743:   return pc;
744: }
745: 
746: /* Return the current value of the stack pointer */
747: 
748: static inline_function uintptr_t up_getsp(void)
749: {
750:   register uintptr_t sp;
751:   __asm__
752:   (
753:     "\tadd  %0, x0, x2\n"
754:     : "=r"(sp)
755:   );
756:   return sp;
757: }

873: noinstrument_function static inline_function irqstate_t up_irq_save(void)
874: {

877:   /* Read mstatus & clear machine interrupt enable (MIE) in mstatus */

879:   __asm__ __volatile__

882:       : "=r" (flags)
883:       : "r"(STATUS_IE)
884:       : "memory"
885:     );

887:   /* Return the previous mstatus value so that it can be restored with
888:    * up_irq_restore().

16: /* T-Head E907 扩展 CSR */
17: 
18: #define CSR_MXSTATUS     0x7C0
19: #define CSR_MEXSTATUS    0x7C1
20: #define CSR_MSTATUS      0x300

25:  * SystemInit (来源: luban-lite system.c)
26:  * 由 startup.S 在 BSS 清零后调用
27:  ****************************************************************************/

29: void SystemInit(void)
30: {
31:   /* 使能 mstatus FS (FPU) */
32: 
33:   uint32_t mstatus;
34:   __asm__ __volatile__("csrr %0, mstatus" : "=r"(mstatus));
35:   mstatus |= (1 << 13);  /* FS = 01 (Initial) */
36:   __asm__ __volatile__("csrw mstatus, %0" :: "r"(mstatus));
37: 
38:   /* 使能 mxstatus THEADISAEE (T-Head ISA 扩展) */
39: 
40:   uint32_t mxstatus;
41:   __asm__ __volatile__("csrr %0, 0x7C0" : "=r"(mxstatus));
42:   mxstatus |= (1 << 22);  /* THEADISAEE */
43:   mxstatus |= (1 << 15);  /* MM (Memory Management) */
44:   __asm__ __volatile__("csrw 0x7C0, %0" :: "r"(mxstatus));
45: 
46:   /* 使能 mexstatus SPUSHEN/SPSWAPEN */
47: 
48:   uint32_t mexstatus;
49:   __asm__ __volatile__("csrr %0, 0x7C1" : "=r"(mexstatus));
50:   mexstatus |= (1 << 16);  /* SPUSHEN */
51:   mexstatus |= (1 << 17);  /* SPSWAPEN */
52:   __asm__ __volatile__("csrw 0x7C1, %0" :: "r"(mexstatus));
53: }

97: void d13x_clock_init(void)
98: {
99:   uint32_t reg;
100: 
101:   /* 打开 24MHz 振荡器 */
102: 
103:   reg = getreg32(CMU_BASE + 0x0A4);
104:   reg |= (1 << 1);
105:   putreg32(reg, CMU_BASE + 0x0A4);
106: 
107:   /* PLL 公共电路 LDO */
108: 
109:   reg = getreg32(CMU_BASE + 0x0A0);
110:   reg |= (1 << 31) | (1 << 0);
111:   putreg32(reg, CMU_BASE + 0x0A0);
112: 
113:   /* PLL_INT1 → 1.2GHz */
114: 
115:   putreg32(0x240C4040, CMU_BASE + 0x044);
116:   while (!(getreg32(CMU_BASE + 0x044) & (1 << 17)));
117: 
118:   /* PLL_INT0 → 480MHz */
119: 
120:   putreg32(0x240C4040, CMU_BASE + 0x040);
121:   while (!(getreg32(CMU_BASE + 0x040) & (1 << 17)));
122: 
123:   /* 总线时钟 */
124: 
125:   putreg32(0x00000001, CMU_BASE + 0x100);
126:   putreg32(0x00000001, CMU_BASE + 0x120);
127:   putreg32(0x00000100, CMU_BASE + 0x200);
128: 
129:   /* GPIO/UART 时钟 */
130: 
131:   reg = getreg32(CMU_BASE + 0x83C);
132:   reg |= (1 << 12) | (1 << 13);
133:   putreg32(reg, CMU_BASE + 0x83C);
134:   putreg32(0x00001001, CMU_BASE + 0x840);
135: 
136:   /* QSPI0 时钟: 释放复位 + 使能总线时钟 + 使能模块时钟 */
137: 
138:   putreg32((1 << 13) | (1 << 12) | (1 << 8), CMU_BASE + 0x460);
139: }

149:   putreg32(divisor & 0xFF, UART0_BASE + 0x00);  /* DLL */
150:   putreg32((divisor >> 8) & 0xFF, UART0_BASE + 0x04);  /* DLH */
151:   putreg32(0x07, UART0_BASE + 0x08);        /* FIFO: enable + reset */
152:   putreg32(0x03, UART0_BASE + 0x0C);        /* LCR: 8N1 */

173:  * QSPI 控制器 (D13x)

185: #define QSPI_CCFG      (QSPI_BASE + 0x024)
186: #define QSPI_TXD       (QSPI_BASE + 0x200)
187: #define QSPI_RXD       (QSPI_BASE + 0x300)
188: 
189: /* QSPI_CFG bits */
190: 
191: #define QSPI_CFG_EN        (1 << 0)
192: #define QSPI_CFG_MASTER    (1 << 1)
193: #define QSPI_CFG_RST       (1 << 31)
194: 
195: /* QSPI_TCFG bits */
196: 
197: #define QSPI_TCFG_CPHA     (1 << 0)
198: #define QSPI_TCFG_CPOL     (1 << 1)
199: #define QSPI_TCFG_CS_LOW   (0 << 7)
200: #define QSPI_TCFG_CS_HIGH  (1 << 7)
201: #define QSPI_TCFG_CS_SW    (1 << 6)
202: #define QSPI_TCFG_START    (1 << 31)
203: 
204: /* QSPI_FSTS bits */
205: 
206: #define QSPI_FSTS_TD       (1 << 12)
207: #define QSPI_FSTS_TF_EMP   (1 << 5)
208: #define QSPI_FSTS_RF_RDY   (1 << 0)

210: static void d13x_spi_init(void)
211: {
212:   /* 复位控制器 */
213: 
214:   putreg32(QSPI_CFG_RST, QSPI_CFG);
215:   while (getreg32(QSPI_CFG) & QSPI_CFG_RST);
216: 
217:   /* 使能控制器 + 主机模式 */
218: 
219:   putreg32(QSPI_CFG_EN | QSPI_CFG_MASTER, QSPI_CFG);
220: 
221:   /* 时钟分频: SPI_CLK = src_clk / (2 * (CKDIV2 + 1))
222:    * src=480MHz, CKDIV2=15 → SPI_CLK = 480/(2*16) = 15MHz */
223: 
224:   putreg32(15, QSPI_CCFG);
225: 
226:   /* 传输配置: Mode 0 (CPOL=0, CPHA=0), 软件控制CS */
227: 
228:   putreg32(QSPI_TCFG_CS_SW | QSPI_TCFG_CS_HIGH, QSPI_TCFG);
229: 
230:   /* 复位 FIFO */
231: 
232:   putreg32((1 << 31) | (1 << 15), QSPI_FCTL);
233: }

235: static void d13x_spi_cs(int assert)
236: {
237:   uint32_t reg = getreg32(QSPI_TCFG);
238:   if (assert)
239:     reg &= ~QSPI_TCFG_CS_HIGH;
240:   else
241:     reg |= QSPI_TCFG_CS_HIGH;
242:   putreg32(reg, QSPI_TCFG);
243: }

245: static void d13x_spi_txrx(uint8_t *tx, uint8_t *rx, int len)
246: {
247:   int i;
248:   for (i = 0; i < len; i++)
249:     {
250:       /* 写入 TX FIFO */
251: 
252:       putreg32(tx ? tx[i] : 0, QSPI_TXD);
253: 
254:       /* 启动传输 */
255: 
256:       uint32_t tcfg = getreg32(QSPI_TCFG);
257:       putreg32(tcfg | QSPI_TCFG_START, QSPI_TCFG);
258: 
259:       /* 等待传输完成 */
260: 
261:       while (!(getreg32(QSPI_FSTS) & QSPI_FSTS_TD));
262: 
263:       /* 清除 TD 标志 (W1C) */
264: 
265:       putreg32(QSPI_FSTS_TD, QSPI_ISTS);
266: 
267:       /* 读取 RX FIFO */
268: 
269:       if (rx)
270:         rx[i] = (uint8_t)getreg32(QSPI_RXD);
271:     }
272: }

static int d13x_uart_setup(FAR struct uart_dev_s *dev)
{
  uint32_t divisor;
  divisor = D13X_UART0_FREQ / (16 * D13X_UART0_BAUDRATE);

  putreg32(0, D13X_UART0_BASE + UART_LCR);          // LCR=0 → DLAB=0
  putreg32(divisor & 0xFF, D13X_UART0_BASE + UART_RBR_THR_DLL);  // Writing DLL when DLAB=0 → writing to THR!
  putreg32((divisor >> 8) & 0xFF, D13X_UART0_BASE + UART_DLH);   // Writing DLH when DLAB=0 → writing to IER!

  putreg32(0x03, D13X_UART0_BASE + UART_LCR);
  return OK;
}
```

Wait, this writes LCR=0 first, which sets DLAB=0. Then it tries to write to DLL (at offset 0x00) and DLH (at offset 0x04). But with DLAB=0:

767: /*
768:  * txlen: All tx data byte length in this transfer
769:  * tx_1line_cnt: How much tx bytes using 1 line to send out in this transfer
770:  * rxlen: All rx data byte length in this transfer
771:  * dmy_cnt: How much dummy bytes need hardware to generate and send out
772:  */
773: static inline void qspi_hw_set_transfer_cnt(u32 base, u32 txlen, u32 tx_1line_cnt, u32 rxlen,
774:                                             u32 hw_dmy_cnt)
775: {
776:     u32 val = readl(QSPI_REG_TBC(base));
777: 
778:     /* Total transfer byte count */
779:     val &= ~(TBC_BIT_TB_CNT_MSK);
780:     val |= TBC_BIT_TB_CNT_VAL(txlen + rxlen + hw_dmy_cnt);
781:     writel(val, QSPI_REG_TBC(base));
782: 
783:     /* Total write data length */
784:     val = readl(QSPI_REG_TWC(base));
785:     val &= ~(TWC_BIT_TXD_CNT_MSK);
786:     val |= TWC_BIT_TXD_CNT_VAL(txlen);
787:     writel(val, QSPI_REG_TWC(base));
788: 
789:     /*
790:      * Special configuration:
791:      * # Data length need to send in single mode
792:      *   - If the transfer is already single mode, the tx_1line_cnt should be
793:      *     the same with total send data length
794:      *   - If the transfer is DUAL/QUAD mode, the tx_1line_cnt specifies the length
795:      *     that need to send out in single mode, usually for cmd,addr,...
796:      * # Dummy count for DUAL/QUAD mode
797:      *   - DMY_CNT specifies how many dummy burst should be sent before receive
798:      *     data in DUAL/QUAD mode
799:      */
800:     val = readl(QSPI_REG_TMC(base));
801:     val &= ~(TMC_BIT_STXD_CNT_MSK);
802:     val |= TMC_BIT_STXD_CNT_VAL(tx_1line_cnt);
803:     val &= ~(TMC_BIT_DMY_CNT_MSK);
804:     val |= TMC_BIT_DMY_CNT_VAL(hw_dmy_cnt);
805:     writel(val, QSPI_REG_TMC(base));
806: }

The chip.h is missing several registers that the reference HAL code (`aic_hal_uart.c`) uses and the User Manual documents:

| Missing Register | Offset | Used By HAL? | Severity |
|-----------------|--------|-------------|----------|
| `UART_USR` | 0x7C | Yes (busy check) | **HIGH** |
| `UART_HALT` | 0xA4 | Yes (baudrate config) | **MEDIUM** |
| `UART_SCH` | 0x1C | No | Low |

### 3. ISSUE #1 (CRITICAL): DLAB/Divisor Setup is Wrong in `d13x_uart_setup()`

**File:** `artinchip_uart.c`, lines 44-58

The code writes LCR=0 first, then attempts to write DLL and DLH. But the User Manual (line 96062-96066) is unambiguous:

> "If DLAB is 0, offset 0x00 is TX/RX FIFO, offset 0x04 is IER register."
> "If DLAB is 1, offset 0x00 is DLL, offset 0x04 is DLH."

The current sequence:
```
putreg32(0, ... + UART_LCR);                    // LCR=0 → DLAB=0
putreg32(divisor & 0xFF, ... + UART_RBR_THR_DLL); // writing THR, NOT DLL!
putreg32((divisor >> 8) & 0xFF, ... + UART_DLH);  // writing IER, NOT DLH!
putreg32(0x03, ... + UART_LCR);                   // 8N1, but divisor never set
```

With DLAB=0, offset 0x00 maps to THR (write) and offset 0x04 maps to IER. The divisor values are written to the wrong registers entirely. The baud rate divisor is never actually programmed.

**Correct sequence** (as demonstrated by the reference HAL at `aic_hal_uart.c` lines 149-159):
```
putreg32(LCR_DLAB, ... + UART_LCR);    // LCR[7]=1 → DLAB=1
putreg32(divisor & 0xFF, ... + UART_RBR_THR_DLL);  // NOW writing DLL
putreg32((divisor >> 8) & 0xFF, ... + UART_DLH);   // NOW writing DLH
putreg32(0x03, ... + UART_LCR);         // Set 8N1, clear DLAB
```

---

### 4. ISSUE #2 (HIGH): No USR Busy Check Before Register Writes

The User Manual explicitly requires checking `USR[0]` (BUSY) before writing LCR and divisor registers. Five separate LCR bit descriptions (lines 97116, 97164, 97183, 97196, 97212) state:

> "仅当 UART 空闲时（USR[0] 为 0）此位才可写" (This bit can only be written when UART is idle, USR[0]=0)

And for DLL/DLH (lines 96512-96513, 96564-96565):

> "仅当 DLAB 位 (LCR[7]) 为 1 并且 UART 空闲 (USR[0]) 时，该寄存器才能被访问"

The reference HAL (`aic_hal_uart.c` line 31) has the `WAIT_USART_IDLE` macro that polls `addr->USR & USR_UART_BUSY` with a timeout before any register configuration. The NuttX driver in `d13x_uart_setup()` performs zero USR checks.

Additionally, `UART_USR` is not even defined in `chip.h`, so the driver has no way to perform this check.

---

### 5. ISSUE #3 (MEDIUM): RX Interrupt Enable Logic Uses Wrong Register Offset

**File:** `artinchip_uart.c`, lines 91-107

The `d13x_uart_rxint()` function reads and writes `UART_DLH` (offset 0x04) to manipulate interrupt enable bits. This works *only* when DLAB=0, because with DLAB=0, offset 0x04 maps to IER. However:

- There is no code ensuring DLAB=0 before accessing this register.
- After `d13x_uart_setup()` sets LCR=0x03 (which clears DLAB), the function should work correctly **if** the setup had been done properly. But there is no guard.
- The HAL code (`aic_hal_uart.c` lines 343-361) manipulates IER directly via `addr->IER |= flag` / `addr->IER &= ~flag`, which is a struct-based access that is DLAB-independent.

The bit masks are correct per the User Manual:
- `IER[0]` = ERBFI (RX Data Available Interrupt Enable) -- the code uses `0x01` which matches.
- `IER[1]` = ETBEI (TX Holding Register Empty Interrupt Enable) -- not defined in chip.h.

### 6. ISSUE #4 (MEDIUM): `d13x_uart_send()` Waits for THRE but Does Not Check USR Before Writing THR

**File:** `artinchip_uart.c`, lines 114-118

The send function polls `UART_LSR & UART_LSR_THRE` before writing THR. This is the standard 16550 pattern and is correct per the User Manual (line 96474): "串行输出端口发送的数据，仅当线路状态寄存器 (LSR) 中的 THRE 位 (LSR[5]) 被设为 1 时，数据才会写到该寄存器。"

**File:** `artinchip_lowputc.c`, lines 29-38

The low-level put character function polls THRE then writes THR directly, without any USR busy check. Same hardware bug concern as issue #4.

The `d13x_uart_attach()` function calls `irq_attach()` and `up_enable_irq()` but never disables stale interrupts via IER before enabling the IRQ line. The reference HAL (`aic_hal_uart.c` line 715) zeroes IER (`addr->IER = 0`) during initialization before attaching the handler.

### 9. ISSUE #7 (LOW): `d13x_uart_handler()` Reads Into Local Variable and Discards

**File:** `artinchip_uart.c`, lines 29-35

The ISR reads RBR into `volatile uint32_t thr` and then casts it to void. The comment says "读取字符并放入缓冲区" (read character and put into buffer) but the data is never passed to `uart_recvchars()`. text:
Here is the comprehensive difference report across all six areas.

---

## 1. GP Register Initialization

**OpenVela bootloader** (`startup.S` lines 60-65):
```asm
.option push
.option norelax
la      gp, __global_pointer$
.option pop
```

**luban-lite** (`startup_gcc.S` lines 130-135):
```asm
.option push
.option norelax
j       save_boot_params
save_boot_params_ret:
    la      gp, __global_pointer$
.option pop
```

**Differences:**
- Both use the identical GP-init pattern (`la gp, __global_pointer$` wrapped in `.option norelax` / `.option pop`). No functional difference in the GP init itself.
- **Structural difference:** luban-lite sets GP *after* returning from `save_boot_params`, via a `j save_boot_params` / `save_boot_params_ret:` trampoline. The bootloader sets GP directly in the linear flow after BSS clear, with no trampoline. The GP value is correct in both cases.

---

## 2. CSR Writes (mxstatus / mexstatus / mstatus.FS)

**OpenVela bootloader** (`system.c` lines 29-53):
```c
// mstatus.FS always set (no #ifdef)
mstatus |= (1 << 13);  // FS = Initial
// mxstatus always set
mxstatus |= (1 << 22); // THEADISAEE
mxstatus |= (1 << 15); // MM
// mexstatus always set
mexstatus |= (1 << 16); // SPUSHEN
mexstatus |= (1 << 17); // SPSWAPEN
```

**luban-lite** (`system.c` lines 90-120):
```c
// mstatus.FS conditional
#ifdef ARCH_RISCV_FPU
    mstatus |= (1 << 13);
    __set_MSTATUS(mstatus);
#endif
// mxstatus always set (same bits)
mxstatus |= (1 << 22); // THEADISAEE
mxstatus |= (1 << 15); // MM
// mexstatus conditional
#ifdef CONFIG_THEAD_EXT_SPUSHEN
    mexstatus |= (1 << 16); // SPUSHEN
#endif
#ifdef CONFIG_THEAD_EXT_SPSWAPEN
    mexstatus |= (1 << 17); // SPSWAPEN
#endif
```

**Differences:**
1. **mstatus.FS** -- Bootloader sets it unconditionally; luban-lite guards it behind `#ifdef ARCH_RISCV_FPU`. The result is the same if the config is defined, but the bootloader will always enable FPU even if the build config says no FPU.
2. **mexstatus SPUSHEN/SPSWAPEN** -- Bootloader sets both unconditionally; luban-lite guards each behind `CONFIG_THEAD_EXT_SPUSHEN` / `CONFIG_THEAD_EXT_SPSWAPEN`. The bootloader will always enable these features regardless of build config.
3. **CSR access method** -- Bootloader uses raw `csrr`/`csrw` inline asm with hex CSR numbers (`0x7C0`, `0x7C1`). luban-lite uses abstraction macros (`__get_MXSTATUS()` / `__set_MXSTATUS()`). Functionally equivalent.
4. **mxstatus** -- Identical bits set (THEADISAEE bit 22, MM bit 15). No difference.

---

## 3. .data Section Copy

**OpenVela bootloader** (`startup.S`): **No .data copy at all.** The startup code only clears BSS. There is no reference to `__erodata`, `__data_start__`, or `__data_end__`.

**luban-lite** (`startup_gcc.S` lines 200-214):
```asm
#if defined(QEMU_RUN)
    la      a0, __erodata
    la      a1, __data_start__
    la      a2, __data_end__
    // ... copy loop ...
    jal     dcache_clean
#endif
```

**Differences:**
1. **Bootloader never copies .data from flash to RAM.** This means initialized global/static variables in the bootloader will have value 0 (from BSS clear) rather than their initializers. This is a significant functional gap -- any code relying on initialized data will get wrong values.
2. **luban-lite only copies .data in QEMU mode** (`#if defined(QEMU_RUN)`). On real hardware, luban-lite likely relies on XIP or BROM having already set up the data section. This means neither copies .data on real hardware, but luban-lite at least handles it for QEMU.

---

## 4. mtvec / mtvt Setup

**OpenVela bootloader** (`startup.S`): **No mtvec or mtvt setup at all.** The bootloader does not configure any interrupt vector table. There is no CLIC configuration in the C code either.

**luban-lite** (`startup_gcc.S` lines 136-140):
```asm
la      a0, Default_Handler
ori     a0, a0, 3        // set mode bits to 3 (vectored + CLIC)
csrw    mtvec, a0
la      a0, __Vectors
csrw    mtvt, a0
```
Plus in `SystemInit` (`system.c` lines 122-136):
```c
CLIC->CLICCFG = ...;                    // configure CLIC levels
for (i = 0; i < MAX_IRQn; i++) {       // init all interrupt entries
    CLIC->CLICINT[i].IP = 0;
    CLIC->CLICINT[i].ATTR = 1;         // vector interrupt
}
CLIC->CLICINT[Machine_Software_IRQn].ATTR = 0x3;  // tspend
csi_dcache_enable();
csi_icache_enable();
drv_irq_enable(Machine_Software_IRQn);
_system_init_for_kernel();  // timer, IRQ vectors, etc.
```

**Differences:**
1. **Bootloader has zero interrupt infrastructure.** No mtvec, no mtvt, no CLIC init, no vector table. This is a bare-metal SPL that runs entirely with interrupts disabled.
2. **luban-lite configures a full CLIC environment:** mtvec with mode=3 (vectored), mtvt pointing to the 100-entry `__Vectors` table, CLIC config for priority levels, all interrupt entries initialized, and the Machine_Software interrupt (tspend) enabled.
3. **luban-lite also sets up caches and kernel timers** (GTC, CORET/systick) in SystemInit -- the bootloader does none of this.

---

## 5. Boot Parameter Handling

**OpenVela bootloader** (`startup.S` lines 13-56 + `system.c`):
- Saves a0-a7, s0-s11, sp, ra (22 registers) into a global `boot_params_stash` struct (same layout as luban-lite).
- Additionally copies 256 bytes from the BROM-provided `a1` private_data address into a `boot_arg` global buffer.
- Stores `boot_params_stash` in `.bss` (default section).
- No C-level `boot_param.c` file; no `aic_get_boot_device()` or similar accessor functions.

**luban-lite** (`boot_param_gcc.S` + `boot_param.c` + `boot_param.h`):
- Same 22-register save into `boot_params_stash`.
- `boot_params_stash` is placed in `.data` section explicitly (`__attribute__((section(".data")))`).
- Has a full C API: `aic_get_boot_device()`, `aic_get_boot_reason()`, `aic_get_boot_controller()`, `aic_get_boot_resource()`, `aic_get_boot_image_id()`.
- Boot device/reason/controller are packed into a0 using bit fields (bits [3:0] = device, [7:4] = controller, [11:8] = reason, [15:12] = image_id).
- Has `show_boot_device()` with a static "print once" flag.
- Has `aic_timer_get_us()` using CSR `time` (0xC01) with `>> 2` scaling.
- Also declares `aic_get_boot_resource_from_nand()` (NAND boot support).

**Differences:**
1. **256-byte boot_arg copy** -- Only the bootloader copies private_data (a1 pointed data) into a `boot_arg` buffer. luban-lite does not do this; it only stores the raw register values and provides accessor functions.
2. **Section placement** -- luban-lite explicitly places `boot_params_stash` in `.data`; the bootloader places it in `.bss` (default, no section attribute). This matters because .data requires initialization from flash while .bss is zero-initialized. On luban-lite, since .data copy is only done for QEMU, on real hardware the `.data` placement means `boot_params_stash` might not be valid unless the BROM already set up data. However, the save happens *before* any data copy, so the save writes to the address directly -- the issue is only if the linker places `.data` in a non-writable region.
3. **C API for boot params** -- The bootloader has no C-level accessors. Code must directly access `boot_params_stash` fields. luban-lite provides a clean API layer.
4. **Boot device display** -- Only luban-lite prints the boot device name.

---

## 6. QSPI Register Offsets vs. luban-lite SPI HAL

**OpenVela bootloader** (`system.c` lines 178-187):
| Register | Bootloader Offset | Name |
|----------|------------------|------|
| VER      | +0x000           | QSPI_VER |
| CFG      | +0x004           | QSPI_CFG |
| TCFG     | +0x008           | QSPI_TCFG |
| ICR      | +0x010           | QSPI_ICR |
| ISTS     | +0x014           | QSPI_ISTS |
| FCTL     | +0x018           | QSPI_FCTL |
| FSTS     | +0x01C           | QSPI_FSTS |
| CCFG     | +0x024           | QSPI_CCFG |
| TXD      | +0x200           | QSPI_TXD |
| RXD      | +0x300           | QSPI_RXD |

**luban-lite HAL** (`qspi_hw_v1.1.h` lines 16-42):
| Register | HAL Offset | Name |
|----------|-----------|------|
| VER      | +0x00     | QSPI_REG_VER |
| CFG      | +0x04     | QSPI_REG_CFG |
| TCFG     | +0x08     | QSPI_REG_TCFG |
| ICR      | +0x10     | QSPI_REG_ICR |
| ISTS     | +0x14     | QSPI_REG_ISTS |
| FCTL     | +0x18     | QSPI_REG_FCTL |
| FSTS     | +0x1c     | QSPI_REG_FSTS |
| WCC      | +0x20     | QSPI_REG_WCC |
| CCFG     | +0x24     | QSPI_REG_CCFG |
| TBC      | +0x30     | QSPI_REG_TBC |
| TWC      | +0x34     | QSPI_REG_TWC |
| TMC      | +0x38     | QSPI_REG_TMC |
| BMTC     | +0x40     | QSPI_REG_BMTC |
| BMCLK    | +0x44     | QSPI_REG_BMCLK |
| BMTXD    | +0x48     | QSPI_REG_BMTXD |
| BMRXD    | +0x4c     | QSPI_REG_BMRXD |
| BTR      | +0x50     | QSPI_REG_BTR |
| RCM      | +0x54     | QSPI_REG_RCM |
| WLEN     | +0x60     | QSPI_REG_WRAP_LEN |
| DMC      | +0x88     | QSPI_REG_DMC |
| IDMA_*   | +0x8C-0x9C| QSPI_REG_IDMA_* |
| TXD      | +0x200    | QSPI_REG_TXD |
| RXD      | +0x300    | QSPI_REG_RXD |

**Register offset verdict: The 10 registers the bootloader defines all match the HAL exactly.** VER=0x00, CFG=0x04, TCFG=0x08, ICR=0x10, ISTS=0x14, FCTL=0x18, FSTS=0x1C, CCFG=0x24, TXD=0x200, RXD=0x300. No offset discrepancies.

**Bit-field differences:**

The bootloader defines these bit positions for FSTS:
```c
#define QSPI_FSTS_TD       (1 << 12)    // Transfer Done
#define QSPI_FSTS_TF_EMP   (1 << 5)     // TX FIFO Empty
#define QSPI_FSTS_RF_RDY   (1 << 0)     // RX FIFO Ready
```

The HAL defines these for ISTS (interrupt status, same register at +0x14):
```c
ISTS_BIT_TDONE  = (1UL << 12)   // Transfer Done -- MATCHES bootloader's TD bit
ISTS_BIT_TF_EMP = (1UL << 5)    // TX FIFO Empty -- MATCHES
ISTS_BIT_RF_RDY = (1UL << 0)    // RX FIFO Ready -- MATCHES
```

**However, the bootloader has a bug in `d13x_spi_txrx()`** (line 265):
```c
putreg32(QSPI_FSTS_TD, QSPI_ISTS);  // clears TD flag in ISTS register
```
The bootloader clears the TD flag by writing to `QSPI_ISTS` (+0x14). In the HAL, `qspi_hw_clear_interrupt_status()` also writes to `ISTS` (+0x14) with W1C semantics. So this is **correct** -- ISTS is W1C. But note the naming mismatch: the bootloader calls the TD bit "FSTS" (in FSTS register at +0x1C) when it actually writes to ISTS (+0x14). The bit position (12) is the same in both registers, but the semantic naming is misleading in the bootloader.

**Missing registers in bootloader:** The bootloader does not define WCC (+0x20), TBC (+0x30), TWC (+0x34), TMC (+0x38), BMTC/BMCLK/BMTXD/BMRXD (+0x40-0x4C), BTR (+0x50), RCM (+0x54), WLEN (+0x60), DMC (+0x88), or any IDMA registers (+0x8C-0x9C). This limits the bootloader to basic single-line SPI only, with no support for dual/quad mode, burst transfers, bit-mode, or DMA.

**FCTL usage difference:** The bootloader writes `(1 << 31) | (1 << 15)` to FCTL for FIFO reset. In the HAL, bit 31 = `FCTL_BIT_TF_RST` and bit 15 = `FCTL_BIT_RF_RST`. The values match exactly.

**Additional HAL features missing from bootloader:**
- No TX/RX DMA support
- No bit-mode SPI (BMTC/BMCLK/BMTXD/BMRXD registers)
- No burst transfer support (BTR)
- No read-command mode (RCM)
- No XIP support via QSPI (the bootloader does XIP via XSPI for PSRAM only)
- No internal DMA (IDMA) support
- No clock divider selection between CKDIV1/CKDIV2 (bootloader always uses CCFG directly with CKDIV2 value 15, while HAL has `qspi_hw_set_clk_div()` with divider selection)

---

## Summary of All Differences

| Area | Difference | Severity |
|------|-----------|----------|
| **GP init** | Identical logic, different code structure (trampoline vs linear) | None (cosmetic) |
| **mstatus.FS** | Bootloader: unconditional. luban-lite: `#ifdef ARCH_RISCV_FPU` | Low (bootloader always enables FPU) |
| **mexstatus SPUSHEN/SPSWAPEN** | Bootloader: unconditional. luban-lite: `#ifdef CONFIG_THEAD_EXT_*` | Low (bootloader always enables) |
| **mxstatus** | Identical bits set | None |
| **CSR access** | Raw CSR numbers vs abstraction macros | None (cosmetic) |
| **.data copy** | Bootloader: none. luban-lite: only in QEMU mode | Medium (initialized globals broken in both on real HW, but bootloader never handles it) |

# PSRAM Initialization Verification Report

## DISCREPANCY 1 (CRITICAL): XSPI Register Map Is Entirely Wrong in OpenVela

The OpenVela code defines a fabricated register layout at offsets 0x100-0x118 that has **no correspondence** to actual hardware registers.

**Official D13x User Manual (Table 9-15) and luban-lite HAL register map:**

| Offset | Manual Name | luban-lite HAL Name | Function |
|--------|------------|---------------------|----------|
| 0x000 | XSPI_CTL | XSPI_REG_CTL | Control |
| 0x004 | XSPI_CLK | XSPI_REG_CLK | Clock divider |
| 0x008 | XSPI_TCR | XSPI_REG_TCR | Transmit control |
| 0x00C | XSPI_STAS | XSPI_REG_STAS | Status |
| 0x010 | XSPI_CS0_CTL | XSPI_REG_CSO_CTL | CS0 control |
| 0x014 | XSPI_CS0_DCTL | XSPI_REG_CS0_DCTL | CS0 DLL control |
| 0x018 | XSPI_CS1_CTL | XSPI_REG_CS1_CTL | CS1 control |
| 0x01C | XSPI_CS1_DCTL | XSPI_REG_CS1_DCTL | CS1 DLL control |
| 0x020 | XSPI_IER | XSPI_REG_IER | Interrupt enable |
| 0x024 | XSPI_ISR | XSPI_REG_ISR | Interrupt status |
| 0x028 | XSPI_FCR | XSPI_REG_FCR | FIFO control |
| 0x02C | XSPI_FSR | XSPI_REG_FSR | FIFO status |
| 0x030 | XSPI_START | XSPI_REG_START | LUT start trigger |
| 0x034 | XSPI_ADDR | XSPI_REG_ADDR | Address config |
| 0x038 | XSPI_FMR | XSPI_REG_FMR | Format config |
| 0x040 | XSPI_BTR | XSPI_REG_BTR | Burst type |
| 0x044 | XSPI_RCC | XSPI_REG_RCC | Read cmd control |
| 0x048 | XSPI_NDMA_MODE_CTL | XSPI_REG_NDMA_MODE_CTL | DMA mode |
| 0x050 | XSPI_TO | XSPI_REG_TO | Timeout |
| 0x054 | XSPI_LCKCR | XSPI_REG_LCKCR | LUT lock |
| 0x058 | XSPI_LUT_UP | XSPI_REG_LUT_UP | LUT update |
| 0x060 | XSPI_CS0_SEQUENCE | XSPI_REG_CS0_SEQUENCE | CS0 sequence |
| 0x064 | XSPI_CS1_SEQUENCE | XSPI_REG_CS1_SEQUENCE | CS1 sequence |
| 0x068 | XSPI_IO_CTL | XSPI_REG_IO_CTL | IO control |
| 0x100 | XSPI_LUTn (base) | XSPI_REG_LUTN | Look-Up Table entries |
| 0x200 | XSPI_TDR | XSPI_REG_TDR | TX data register |
| 0x300 | XSPI_RDR | XSPI_REG_RDR | RX data register |
| 0xFFC | VERSION | XSPI_REG_VERSION | Version |

**OpenVela code (both files) defines:**

| Offset | OpenVela Name | Actual Hardware |
|--------|--------------|-----------------|
| 0x000 | XSPI_CFG | XSPI_CTL |
| 0x004 | XSPI_TIMING | XSPI_CLK |
| 0x008 | XSPI_CFG2 | XSPI_TCR |
| 0x100 | XSPI_CMD | **XSPI_LUTn[0]** -- NOT a CMD register! |
| 0x104 | XSPI_ADDR | **XSPI_LUTn[1]** -- NOT an ADDR register! |
| 0x108 | XSPI_DATA | **XSPI_LUTn[2]** -- NOT a DATA register! |
| 0x10C | XSPI_CFG3 | **XSPI_LUTn[3]** -- NOT a CFG3 register! |
| 0x110 | XSPI_STATUS | **XSPI_LUTn[4]** -- NOT a STATUS register! |
| 0x114 | XSPI_CTRL | **XSPI_LUTn[5]** -- NOT a CTRL trigger! |
| 0x118 | XSPI_BCNT | **XSPI_LUTn[6]** -- NOT a byte count register! |

The OpenVela code treats the XSPI as a simple command FIFO controller. The real XSPI is a **LUT-based** controller -- you program command sequences into look-up table entries, then trigger them. There are no "CMD", "DATA", "BCNT", "STATUS", or "CTRL" registers at offsets 0x100-0x118.

---

## DISCREPANCY 2 (CRITICAL): XSPI Status Register Bit Interpretation Is Wrong

**Manual (XSPI_STAS at 0x000C):**
- Bit 0: `XSPI_BUSY` -- set when a transfer is in progress
- Bit 1: `AXI_TRANS` -- set when AXI channel is transferring
- Bit 2: `AHB_TRANS` -- set when AHB channel is transferring

**OpenVela code:**
```c
#define XSPI_STATUS_BUSY    (1 << 0)   // Correct -- maps to XSPI_BUSY
#define XSPI_STATUS_DONE    (1 << 1)   // WRONG -- bit 1 is AXI_TRANS, NOT "DONE"
```

The `d13x_xspi_wait_done()` function polls bit 1 as a "DONE" flag, but bit 1 is actually `AXI_TRANS`. There is **no "DONE" bit** in XSPI_STAS. The luban-lite code polls bit 0 (BUSY) going low to detect completion, which is the correct approach:
```c
static inline u8 xspi_hw_check_idle_status(u32 base)
{
    return (readl(XSPI_REG_STAS(base)) & STAS_BIT_BUSY_MSK);  // bit 0 only
}
```

---

## DISCREPANCY 3 (CRITICAL): XSPI Control Register Bit Definitions Are Wrong

**Manual (XSPI_CTL at 0x000):**
- Bit 0: `XSPI_EN` -- module enable
- Bit 1: `IDL_LOW_POWER_EN` -- idle low power
- Bit 2: `XIP_EN` -- XIP mode enable
- Bit 3: `AXI_WRAP_BURST_CTL`
- Bits 4-5: `XSPI_MODE_SEL` (0=Xccela, 1=Hyperbus, 2=OPI, 3=SPI)
- Bit 6: `PARALLEL_MODE`
- Bit 7: `TIMEOUT_EN`
- Bit 8: `Reset_level` (default=1)
- Bit 9: `Reset_en`

**OpenVela code defines:**
```c
#define XSPI_CFG_EN         (1 << 0)   // Maps to XSPI_EN -- correct
#define XSPI_CFG_RST        (1 << 1)   // WRONG -- bit 1 is IDL_LOW_POWER_EN, not reset
#define XSPI_CFG_CLK_EN     (1 << 2)   // WRONG -- bit 2 is XIP_EN, not clock enable
```

The `d13x_xspi_init()` function does:
```c
putreg32(XSPI_CFG_RST, XSPI_CFG);    // Writes 0x02 (IDL_LOW_POWER_EN=1) expecting reset
while (getreg32(XSPI_CFG) & XSPI_CFG_RST);  // Polls bit 1 -- will hang or false-pass
```

The real XSPI has no software reset bit in XSPI_CTL. The official code resets by calling `xspi_hw_reset()` which writes 0 to XSPI_CTL.

---

## DISCREPANCY 4 (CRITICAL): XIP Enable Uses Wrong Bits

**luban-lite code (`xspi_hw_set_xip_en`):**
```c
val |= CTL_BIT_XIP_EN_VAL(en);  // Sets bit 2 (XIP_EN)
```

**OpenVela code (`d13x_psram_xip_enable`):**
```c
cfg |= (1 << 8);  // Comment says "XIP mode" but bit 8 is Reset_level!
cfg |= (1 << 9);  // Comment says "DDR mode" but bit 9 is Reset_en!
```

This writes to the Reset_level and Reset_en bits instead of XIP_EN (bit 2). The XIP mode will never actually be enabled, and the PSRAM device will not be memory-mapped.

---

## DISCREPANCY 5 (CRITICAL): Wrong CMU Clock Register for XSPI

**User Manual:**
- `CLK_XSPI` at CMU_BASE + **0x45C** (XSPI clock)
- `CLK_QSPI0` at CMU_BASE + **0x460** (QSPI0 clock, for SPI Flash)

**OpenVela PSRAM init code (both files):**
```c
/* 1. 使能 XSPI 时钟 (CMU_BASE + 0x460) */
uint32_t reg = getreg32(CMU_BASE + 0x460);  // WRONG -- this is CLK_QSPI0!
reg |= (1 << 13) | (1 << 12) | (1 << 8);
putreg32(reg, CMU_BASE + 0x460);
```

The comment says "enable XSPI clock" but the code writes to **0x460 (CLK_QSPI0)** instead of **0x45C (CLK_XSPI)**. This enables the QSPI0 (SPI Flash) clock module instead of the XSPI (PSRAM) clock module. The XSPI controller will have no clock and will not function.

---

## DISCREPANCY 6 (MAJOR): XSPI Protocol Mode Not Configured

**luban-lite init sequence (`hal_xspi_init`):**
```c
xspi_hw_set_xspi_mode(base, opi);  // Set XSPI_CTL[5:4] = 2 (OPI mode)
xspi_hw_set_clk_div(base, 0, 0);   // Configure clock divider
xspi_hw_set_cs_write_hold(base, 8); // Configure TCR write hold
xspi_hw_set_cs_read_hold(base, 2);  // Configure TCR read hold
xspi_hw_set_wrap_burst_split(base, 1); // Enable wrap burst split
xspi_hw_set_boudary_ctl(base, xspi_1k); // Set boundary control
xspi_hw_set_cs_iocfg(base, cs0, 0x36363636, 0x36363636, 0x36363636, 0x37);
xspi_hw_set_dll_ctl(base, cs0, ICP_150_200M, xspi_d_90b); // DLL config
xspi_hw_set_xspi_en(base, 1); // Enable XSPI module
```

**OpenVela init sequence:** None of these steps are performed. The OpenVela code:
- Does not set the XSPI protocol mode (Xccela/OPI/SPI)
- Does not configure clock dividers (XSPI_CLK)
- Does not configure CS write/read hold (XSPI_TCR)
- Does not configure IO drive strength (IOCFG registers)
- Does not configure DLL settings (CS0_DCTL / CS1_DCTL)
- Does not enable wrap burst split

---

## DISCREPANCY 7 (MAJOR): XIP Protocol Configuration Is Missing

**luban-lite XIP setup (`aic_xspi_psram_xip`):**
The official code configures a full protocol descriptor for XIP:
```c
psram_proto_cfg.mode = XSPI_MODE_OPI;
psram_proto_cfg.clk_mode = XSPI_DDR_MODE;
psram_proto_cfg.wr_cmd_val = 0x80;      // write command
psram_proto_cfg.rd_cmd_val = 0x00;       // read command
psram_proto_cfg.addr_width = 3;          // 3-byte address
psram_proto_cfg.wr_dummy = 2;            // write dummy cycles
psram_proto_cfg.rd_dummy = 0x06;         // read dummy cycles
psram_proto_cfg.wr_cnt = 2;              // write burst count
psram_proto_cfg.rd_cnt = 3;              // read burst count
```
This configures **LUT entries 0-3 for write** and **LUT entries 16-19 for read**, using the proper DDR/OPI protocol format. Then calls `xspi_hw_lut_update()` and `xspi_hw_lut_lock_ctl(LUT_LOCK)`.

**OpenVela XIP setup:**
```c
putreg32(0x00000000, XSPI_CFG2);  // "XIP base address" -- wrong register
putreg32(0x00000000, XSPI_CFG3);  // "XIP size" -- wrong register
```
This writes zeros to LUT entries 1 and 2 (not "CFG2" and "CFG3"), which corrupts the LUT table. No protocol configuration, no read/write LUT entries, no LUT update, no LUT lock.

---

## DISCREPANCY 8 (MAJOR): No DLL/Training Phase

**luban-lite init includes DLL training:**
```c
xspi_hw_set_dll_ctl(base, cs0, ICP_150_200M, xspi_d_90b);
xspi_hw_set_dll_ctl(base, cs1, ICP_150_200M, xspi_d_90b);
// ... then after XIP enable:
aic_xspi_psram_training(&handle, 0, icp_t, psram_buf, len);  // CS0
aic_xspi_psram_training(&handle, 1, icp_t, psram_buf, len);  // CS1
```
Training iterates over DLL phase selections (0-14) to find the optimal sampling point, using memory test patterns.

**OpenVela:** No DLL configuration and no training phase. PSRAM access may fail at higher clock rates without proper DLL calibration.

---

## DISCREPANCY 9 (MAJOR): Missing CS1 Initialization

**luban-lite init:**
```c
hal_xspi_set_cs(&handle, 0);
aic_xspi_psram_dev_reset(&handle);
aic_udelay(100);
aic_xspi_psram_dev_init(&handle);

hal_xspi_set_cs(&handle, 1);  // Also initialize CS1
aic_xspi_psram_dev_reset(&handle);
aic_udelay(100);
aic_xspi_psram_dev_init(&handle);
```

**OpenVela:** Only initializes CS0. CS1 is never configured. If a second PSRAM chip is present, it will not be initialized.

---

## DISCREPANCY 10 (MODERATE): No Delay After PSRAM Reset

**luban-lite:** `aic_udelay(100)` after device reset.
**OpenVela:** No delay between reset command and device init. PSRAM devices require time after reset to complete internal initialization. Skipping the delay can cause mode register writes to fail.

---

## DISCREPANCY 11 (MODERATE): Missing XSPI Mode Selection for PSRAM Commands

The luban-lite PSRAM commands (reset, read MR, write MR) use LUT-based transfers via `hal_xspi_transfer_cpu_sync()`. The OpenVela code attempts to use direct register writes at fabricated offsets. Even if the register offsets were correct, the XSPI controller requires LUT configuration before any AHB command can be executed.

---

## DISCREPANCY 12 (MINOR): Both OpenVela Files Are Internally Consistent

The artinchip_start.c and d13x-bootloader system.c files define identical (equally wrong) XSPI register layouts and identical PSRAM init sequences. The discrepancies between these two files are:

1. **system.c** defines two additional registers: `XSPI_ACNT` (0x11C) and `XSPI_DMA` (0x200). artinchip_start.c does not.
2. **system.c** defines two additional PSRAM commands: `PSRAM_CMD_WRITE` (0x80) and `PSRAM_CMD_READ` (0x00). artinchip_start.c does not.
3. **system.c** defines additional mode registers: `PSRAM_MR1` (0x01) and `PSRAM_MR2` (0x02). artinchip_start.c does not.
4. **system.c** has PSRAM chip ID defines. artinchip_start.c does not.

These additional definitions in system.c are closer to what would be needed, but the register offsets remain wrong.

---

## Summary of Discrepancies by Severity

### CRITICAL (will cause boot failure or incorrect hardware behavior):
1. **XSPI register map is fabricated** -- offsets 0x100-0x118 are LUT registers, not CMD/DATA/STATUS/CTRL
2. **Status register bit 1 is "AXI_TRANS", not "DONE"** -- polling will never detect completion correctly
3. **Control register bit definitions wrong** -- bit 1 is IDL_LOW_POWER_EN (not RST), bit 2 is XIP_EN (not CLK_EN)
4. **XIP enable uses bits 8/9 instead of bit 2** -- XIP will never be enabled; Reset_level/Reset_en will be clobbered
5. **Wrong CMU clock register** -- 0x460 (CLK_QSPI0) is used instead of 0x45C (CLK_XSPI); XSPI gets no clock

### MAJOR (init will complete but PSRAM will not function correctly):
6. **No protocol mode configuration** -- XSPI_MODE_SEL never set; controller defaults to Xccela mode (0) which may not match PSRAM
7. **No XIP LUT configuration** -- write/read LUT entries never programmed; memory-mapped access will send garbage
8. **No DLL training** -- no DLL configuration or phase training; access unreliable at any non-trivial clock speed
9. **No CS1 initialization** -- dual-die PSRAM configurations will fail

### MODERATE:
10. **No delay after PSRAM reset** -- timing violation
11. **No proper AHB/XIP transfer mechanism** -- direct register writes to LUT space will corrupt the look-up table
12. **Missing features in artinchip_start.c** (minor, both files equally broken for the same root cause)

---

## Verdict

The OpenVela PSRAM initialization code in both `artinchip_start.c` and `system.c` was written against an **invented register interface** that does not correspond to the actual D13x XSPI hardware. The XSPI controller is a LUT-based design (similar to FlexSPI/NXP i.MX), not a simple command-FIFO controller. Every stage of the PSRAM init -- clock enable, controller reset, command execution, status polling, and XIP setup -- targets wrong register offsets or wrong bit positions. **None of these functions would work on real hardware.** The code must be rewritten to use the LUT-based interface as implemented in the luban-lite HAL (`xspi_hw_v1.0.h` + `hal_xspi.c` + `xspi_psram.c`).

reg |= (1 << 31);
reg |= (1 << 0);

Manual bit mapping for PLL_COM (Section 8.1.5.11, default `0x80000009`):

- Bit 0: `LDO_EN` -- LDO enable (default = 1)

**Verdict: PASS but redundant.** Both bit 31 and bit 0 are already set to 1 in the reset default value `0x80000009`. The read-modify-write is harmless but accomplishes nothing beyond the default. Not a discrepancy, but worth noting as an unnecessary operation.

The code sets bits 31 and 0. According to Section 8.1.5.11 (manual line 22313-22370):

- Bit 8 = 0 --> source = CLK_24M
- DIV = 1 --> output = 24 / 2 = **12 MHz**

- Bit 8: `CPU_CLK_SEL` -- 0 = CLK_24M, 1 = PLL_INT0/(DIV+1)

- Bit 12: `MOD_BUS_EN` -- "0 = OFF, 1 = ON" (bus clock enable)

Section 8.1.5.47 (manual line 25335-25414):
- Bit 13: `MOD_RSTN` -- reset release
- Bit 12: `MOD_BUS_EN` -- bus clock enable

sg2000:    void *riscv_dispatch_irq(uintptr_t vector, uintptr_t *regs)
```

All other ports use `uintreg_t` or `uintptr_t`. Per `/home/lladlam/OpenVela/openvela/nuttx/arch/risc-v/include/types.h` line 80, `uintreg_t` is `uint32_t` on RV32, so this is *binary-compatible* on the D13x E907 (32-bit) core. However, it diverges from the NuttX coding convention and would break if the code were ever ported to an RV64 core.

Additionally, the D13x calls `irq_dispatch(irq, regs)` directly (line 197), whereas most other ports call `riscv_doirq(irq, regs)` which handles context switching. The D13x version returns `regs` directly without going through `riscv_doirq`. This is a functional concern -- `irq_dispatch` dispatches the handler but does not perform the context-switch plumbing that `riscv_doirq` does.

---

## ISSUE 3 — MEDIUM: `up_irq_enable` Implements Non-CLIC Logic But CLIC Is Used

**Location**: `artinchip_irq.c`, lines 210-222

The D13x CLIC interrupt controller is used throughout the file (mtvec mode 3, mtvt, CLICINT registers), and `irq.h` defines `up_irq_save`/`up_irq_restore` to manipulate `CSR_INTTHRESH` when `CONFIG_ARCH_RV_HAVE_CLIC` is set (lines 840-861 of irq.h).

Yet the D13x `up_irq_enable()` manipulates `mstatus` via inline assembly (bit 3 = MIE), which is the non-CLIC path. When `CONFIG_ARCH_RV_HAVE_CLIC` is enabled, interrupt gating should be done through the CLIC threshold CSR (`CSR_INTTHRESH`), not `mstatus.MIE`. The NuttX `irq.h` provides CLIC-aware `up_irq_save`/`up_irq_restore` for exactly this purpose.

If `CONFIG_ARCH_RV_HAVE_CLIC` is not set in the D13x config, the `mstatus` approach works but then the mtvec/mtvt setup in `up_irqinitialize` (using CLIC mode 3) becomes inconsistent -- you cannot use CLIC vectoring without also using CLIC for interrupt masking.

---

## ISSUE 4 — LOW: `up_allocate_heap` Missing `FAR` Qualifier

**Location**: `artinchip_allocateheap.c`, line 38

```
Header:  void up_allocate_heap(FAR void **heap_start, size_t *heap_size)
D13x:    void up_allocate_heap(void **heap_start, size_t *heap_size)
```

The `FAR` macro is `#define FAR` (empty) in flat build, so this compiles identically. However, in kernel/user-space builds (`CONFIG_BUILD_KERNEL` or `CONFIG_BUILD_PROTECTED`), `FAR` resolves to an address-space qualifier. Omitting it is a coding standard violation though functionally benign in the expected flat-build configuration.

---

## ISSUE 5 — LOW: Oneshot `start()` Writes to Counter Register as Comparison Value

**Location**: `artinchip_oneshot.c`, lines 110-117

```c
static void d13x_oneshot_start(struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *lower, clkcnt_t delay)
{
  uint32_t now_lo = getreg32(GTC_CNTVL);
  uint32_t cmp = now_lo + (uint32_t)delay;
  putreg32(cmp, GTC_CNTVL);  /* writes to the counter value register */
}
```

The code writes the comparison target back into `GTC_CNTVL`, which is the *counter value* register (offset 0x0008), not a compare register. There is no separate compare register defined in the GTC register map (lines 26-33). Writing to `GTC_CNTVL` would overwrite the running counter, not set a comparison threshold. This means the timer interrupt may never fire unless the hardware implicitly uses `GTC_CNTVL` as both counter-read and compare-write (some timer controllers do this, but the comments suggest otherwise).

Similarly, `d13x_oneshot_cancel` writes `0xFFFFFFFF` to `GTC_CNTVL` (line 144), which would corrupt the running counter.
